#1942. Biggest Champions League away wins of all time after Lens 1-9 Como

By Darren Plant | 05 Nov 2026 10:29

Como are the talk of Europe after they recorded the biggest away win in Champions League history with a 9-1 victory at Lens.

Cesc Fabregas's reputation had already been enhanced with 4-1 triumphs over RB Leipzig and Manchester United earlier in the 2026-27 league phase, but Como's players have now etched their name in the record books - perhaps permanently - in numerous categories.

While Fabregas's focus has quickly turned back to domestic matters with Como sitting in fourth position in the Serie A table, football fans across the world are reminiscing over the kind of matches that have been pushed down the record books.

Here, Sports Mole provides a rundown of the biggest away victories in the Champions League era, including matches from the group stage or league phase onwards.

Prior to Como's exploits in France, there had been three instances of teams prevailing by 7-0 scorelines on away territory.

Liverpool are the team to have most recently prevailed by that score in October 2017, with Jurgen Klopp overseeing a routine win over NK Maribor in Slovenia with Roberto Firmino and Mohamed Salah both netting doubles.

Three days earlier, Luiz Adriano memorably scored five times for Shakhtar Donetsk in a 7-0 triumph at BATE Borisov of Belarus.

Meanwhile, Marseille were the first-ever 7-0 away victors in Champions League history, having cruised to success over Slovakian side MSK Zilina in 2010.

There are many other occasions where a team has prevailed by a six-goal margin, but Bayern Munich's 8-2 drubbing of Barcelona is the only example of that score for a designated away team.

However, "designated" is the key word here, with the quarter-final tie having taken place on neutral ground in Lisbon in August 2020 due to the coronavirus pandemic.

Some notable names have found themselves on the receiving end of a 7-1 scoreline, including Roma who were thrashed by Pep Guardiola's Bayern Munich at Stadio Olimpico in October 2014.

At six minutes and 12 seconds, Salah scored the fastest Champions League hat-trick in history when Liverpool beat Rangers at Ibrox eight years later.

As recently as March 2025, Arsenal cruised past Dutch giants PSV Eindhoven, while Lyon's trouncing of Dinamo Zagreb - which included four goals for Bafetimbi Gomis - was the first-ever 7-1 away scoreline in Champions League history in December 2011.

#1937. Barcelona: French defender tracked by Arsenal and Chelsea takes step towards move, January deal unlikely

By Axel Clody | 05 Nov 2026 11:23

Castello Lukeba wants to join Barcelona and has taken a step towards the Catalan club. Although Barcelona are looking to sign a centre-back in the next winter transfer window, the arrival of the Frenchman appears unlikely.

Barcelona want to sign a centre-back this winter and have several players in their sights, including Natan and Alessandro Bastoni. Rumours are multiplying about the Catalan club’s search. Sport now reports that Lukeba has been one of the centre-backs attracting the most attention at Barcelona for some time.

The French centre-back wants to leave RB Leipzig soon to join a European heavyweight. To that end, the former Lyon player has decided to change agent. The 23-year-old has signed with Excellence Sport, a choice that is far from insignificant as it is the same agency as Jules Kounde.

The Catalan media outlet indicates that Lukeba wants to join Barcelona and is making a clear step towards the club with this choice.

His new agent already met Deco around ten days ago. However, even if the interest is mutual and the French international is a unanimous choice at Barcelona, a deal is not expected to happen in the next winter transfer window.

Indeed, Leipzig have made it clear that they will not let Lukeba leave mid-season. The financial conditions will not be in place in January either for such an investment by the Spanish champions. The next summer transfer window could be the ideal time, since the Frenchman’s release clause will drop from £68m (€80m) to £55m (€65m) in June 2027.

Chelsea and Arsenal are also reportedly monitoring the Frenchman, whose contract runs until June 2029.

That amount could still be negotiable provided the player clearly expresses his desire to play in Catalonia.

The former Lyon player, who interests several big Premier League clubs, considers Barcelona his ideal destination. ‘For now, contacts have started and Barcelona have put his name in capital letters in case this transfer is possible this summer,’ says Sport.

Lukeba’s arrival at Barcelona this summer could be financed by the departure of Ronald Araujo to Liverpool, as the Reds appear set to trigger his £46m (€55m) purchase option.

Before the next summer window, the Catalan club is therefore looking for another left-footed centre-back who could arrive this winter on reasonable financial terms.

#1936. Celtic player ratings as 9/10 sub duo complete Europa League rescue mission

Started well with a tremendous save to deny Leandro Trossard a wonder goal, before the offside flag was raised. Saved Junior Olaitan's penalty but couldn't track the ball from his stop as the rebound was hammered over the line. Beaten all ends up by Orkun Kokcu's drive to make it 2-2.

A positive performance from the left-back, recalled to Scotland duty after missing out through injury last month. Was so determined in his one-v-one against former Rangers rival Vaclav Cerny. Tried to join the attack where possible and was eventually rewarded as his shot turned into an assist for Camilo Duran's winner.

Becoming a leader for Celtic in defence. Never shirked a duel and had to win a number of key tackles throughout a battling 90 minutes at Parkhead. Was wasteful with the ball a few times and not at his commanding best when Celtic retreated in first half but regrouped after break. So close to scoring with a towering header in second half.

A fairly comfortable evening for the centre-back who was largely on top of Besiktas' attacking output, with Celtic standing up to some serious pressure in spells. A little hesitant in his use of the ball at times but defensively sound throughout. Withdrawn for the closing stages.

An unexpected first start for Celtic but settled into the match pretty well. Earned early praise for his swashbuckling defending and charges forward. A better night for the Celtic captain in Europe. Didn't start particularly well as Celtic struggled to take any control of things but he was relentless in his efforts. But perhaps could have been out quicker to block Kokcu goal.

Had the first shot on target of the evening for Celtic after 50 minutes as he tested Alex Nubel to force the German into a smart stop low to his left. Was largely quiet otherwise in a first half where Celtic were little more than passengers and openings in the final third at a premium.

Another seriously frustrating night for the £11m striker, who looks to be carrying the weight of every pound of his price tag. Too often the ball bounced off him or his link-up play wasn't on point as the ball just kept returning to Besiktas. Rallied in the second half, but recent form was typified by his terrible, wayward pass which ended a threatening move for Celtic.

An outstanding display as he led the rescue mission for Celtic. Was only on the park for 49 seconds before lashing home the leveller. Then teed up Camilo Duran for the second. Brilliant.

Another player to have a huge impact coming off the bench. An absolute livewire from the moment he was introduced, he breathed new life into Celtic's frontline as he was slick with his first strike and showed killer instinct to hit the winner.

Replaced Lotomba after a mixed first start, and immediately assisted Duran and Osmand in upping the tempo for Celtic.

Went close with a fizzing strike from the edge of the box, but it was well beaten clear of goal.

Straight into central defence to partner Scales as Carter-Vickers was withdrawn for the closing stages.

#1934. Plymouth Argyle vs Alvechurch - prediction, team news, lineups

By Calum Burrowes | 05 Nov 2026 11:32, Last updated: 05 Nov 2026 11:42

Reaching the first round of the FA Cup for the second time in three seasons, seventh-tier Alvechurch travel to League One Plymouth Argyle hoping to continue their journey in football's oldest cup competition.

The Pilgrims head into Saturday's clash after a goalless draw with Reading last weekend that kept them in the top five, while the Church have already played five matches to reach this stage, most recently beating Spalding United 4-0 in a replay.

Plymouth Argyle will be hoping to avoid a cup upset on Saturday afternoon when they welcome their Midlands opponents to Home Park.

Tom Cleverley's side, who were knocked out in the first round of the FA Cup last season, head into the weekend in good form, having lost just two of their last seven outings in all competitions.

Since suffering back-to-back league defeats against Huddersfield Town and Stevenage, the Pilgrims have responded with a narrow victory over Cambridge United before sharing the points with Reading in a goalless draw.

After 14 League One matches, Plymouth have collected 23 points and sit comfortably in the playoff places, six points behind the league leaders as they look to mount a serious push for promotion back to the Championship.

The Devon outfit failed to progress beyond the opening round last season but enjoyed runs to the fourth and fifth rounds in the 2023-24 and 2024-25 campaigns, where they were eventually eliminated by Leeds United and Manchester City respectively.

Looking to reach the second round of the FA Cup for the second time in three years, Alvechurch make the journey south hoping some cup magic can help them produce one of the shocks of the season.

The Worcestershire-based side, who compete in the Southern League Premier Division Central, know they face a significant challenge against opponents four tiers above them, but arrive at Home Park in good form.

Led by former Wrexham and Cheltenham Town midfielder Kyle Storer, the Church are currently enjoying an unbeaten run of six matches in all competitions, including an impressive 3-1 away win against Leiston on Halloween and a 4-0 victory over Spalding in their FA Cup replay.

During that run, Storer's side have kept just one clean sheet but found the net 16 times, and will be hoping to showcase their attacking threat against League One opposition this weekend.

So far in this season's FA Cup, Alvechurch have overcome Wolverhampton City, Warwick, Cambridge and Spalding, with the latter requiring a replay after a 2-2 draw in the initial meeting.

As mentioned, the Church have previous experience of causing a cup upset, having beaten League One Cheltenham Town 2-1 away from home in the first round in November 2022, before reaching the second round and falling to Forest Green Rovers.

Ahead of a clash against opponents from several divisions below, Cleverley is likely to name a much-changed lineup and could stick with a similar XI to the one used in the EFL Trophy this season.

Murphy Cooper has been Plymouth's first-choice goalkeeper this season but withdrew from their match against Reading the day before the game due to a family issue.

James Storer came in for his league debut and impressed, meaning he could retain his place between the sticks for this one.

Teenager Sep Campbell, the club's youngest-ever goalscorer, has not featured for Plymouth since an EFL Trophy victory over Newport County but could return to the attack on Saturday.

As for the visitors, they reported no fresh injury concerns following their most recent outing and could name a similar starting XI to the one that secured their place in the next round a few weeks ago.

Miracle Okafor, who scored a brace in their 4-0 victory over Spalding, is likely to lead the line for Storer's men alongside Danny Newton.

Plymouth Argyle possible starting lineup:

Storer; Ross, Mitchell, Rendle; Edwards, Bakinson, White, MacKenzie; Amaechi, Campbell, Evans

Evans; Rask; Forsyth, Crowther, Ngandu, Sullivan; Reilly, Osborne, Stephens; Okafor, Newton

There is an obvious gulf in quality between these sides, and while Alvechurch have already shown they can trouble Football League opposition in the FA Cup, Plymouth should have enough to avoid an upset.

We expect the Pilgrims to progress comfortably into the next round with a 4-1 victory over the Church.

#1933. FC Thun 3 Hearts 1: Another bruising Conference League defeat as injury woes worsen

Depleted Hearts’ Conference League bruising was almost totally self-inflicted in a 3-1 defeat by Thun in Switzerland.

Belgian boss Wouter Vrancken was without 10 players through various ailments and the Scottish outfit were dealt another blow in the 22nd minute when defender Jamie McCart put through his own goal in calamitous fashion.

Thun doubled their lead in the 33rd minute through striker Brighton Labeau after more poor defending, this time from skipper Stephen Kingsley – who went off later with an injury – and then Furkan Dursun grabbed a third in the 56th minute before Jambos defender Stuart Findlay reduced the deficit in the 82nd minute with a header.

Hearts were left with one Conference League point out of nine following a 1-1 home draw against Nordsjaelland and a 2-0 defeat away to Trabzonspor.

Thick smoke from a pyro halted the game soon after kick-off but when play resumed after a lengthy delay – there were nine minutes added on at the end of the first half – Hearts winger Josh McPake drew a save from Niklas Steffen with an angled drive that lacked real power.

In the 20th minute McPake’s effort from 25 yards after he had drifted in from the left had the power but was beaten away by the Thun keeper.

There appeared to be nothing untoward on the horizon but then came a Hearts horror show.

There was no real pressure on the Jambos goal when a long ball came into the box but with Lucien Dahler at his shoulder, a simple pass back from McCart somehow evaded Hearts keeper Beau Reus and slipped into the corner of the net.

Thun’s second goal was also gift-wrapped.

The home side broke clear and with pace following a Heart set-piece and when Nils Reichmuth crossed into the box from the right, Kingsley stuck out a leg to clear but the ball went straight to Labeau who swept it into the net from 10 yards out.

Dursun was shown a yellow card for a forearm challenge into the face of Findlay, and it perhaps deserved more punishment.

The interval gave the Tynecastle side time to reset but three minutes after the break, Reus made a diving save from Dursun and an even better one from Reichmuth moments later.

However, the keeper was beaten once again when Dursun got his toe to a Reichmuth cross.

On the hour mark, Nico Maier raced clear of the Hearts defence but although his chip beat Reus, it sped wide of the target.

The night got worse for the rattled visitors as injured Kingsley was replaced by 19-year-old Matthew Gillies, called back from a loan spell at Stenhousemuir.

Malachi Fagan-Walcott’s header from a Jordi Altena free-kick was brilliantly saved by Steffen.

In the 78th minute Jan Bamert had the ball in the net after Steffen tipped a free-kick from substitute Nassim Zoukit on to the bar but was ruled offside, before Findlay headed in a consolation from another Altena free-kick.

#1932. Mason Mount offering Michael Carrick a midfield solution which could have legs

It is not uncommon to hear football club executives talking about the importance of the “money being on the pitch”.

In other words, managers having their best players fit and available most if not all of the time. Quality at the top level is essential but so is robustness. They go hand in hand.

Unfortunately for Manchester United, the money has not been on the pitch down the years nearly as much as the club would want or expect.

Bruno Fernandes stands out for what he does with the ball primarily, but also because he plays almost every minute of every game and, while his sheer indefatigability is extreme, United know they need more of his ilk.

This is why the forthcoming season is such a big one for Mason Mount. His quality has seldom been in doubt. The problem is he has rarely been on the pitch long or consistently enough to show it.

Indeed, the one-time England midfielder has started just 25 Premier League matches since his £60m move from Chelsea three years ago and that perennial unavailability is one of the reasons doubts were being cast about his Old Trafford future going into this summer.

Yet Michael Carrick was keen to keep Mount, United have rebuffed inquiries around him and intriguingly the 27-year-old could yet have an impact on what the club do during the remaining six weeks of the transfer window.

For the second time in the space of six days, Mount was deployed in a deeper midfield role alongside new £48m, signing Andrey Santos for Friday’s resounding 5-0 victory over Norwegian side Rosenborg in Trondheim, just as he had done against Wrexham last weekend.

Mount has spent the majority of his career playing further forward, either off the right or as a No. 10 but Carrick likes him in a fluid No. 8 role, a position Erik ten Hag had identified for the player only for persistent injuries to detonate those plans.

The logic is simple: Mount is mobile, can cover the ground, is adept under pressure, has line breaking passing, vision and a nose for goal. He is also a good presence in the dressing room and a leader in his own way. Watch him imparting advice to Shea Lacey as they walked back to the centre circle after the youngster’s goal opened the scoring against Rosenborg and you get a glimpse of that.

The question, of course, is whether he can stay fit long enough to impose those qualities that help to explain why Liverpool and Arsenal had also been so keen to sign him back in 2023 and Carrick’s predecessor Ruben Amorim was also such a fan.

With United’s summer budget only stretching so far, Carrick was always going to have to think on his feet in certain areas of the pitch.

What will be interesting to see over the coming weeks is whether the manager feels Mount is robust enough to complement Santos, fellow summer signing Youri Tielemans and Kobbie Mainoo.

MASON MOUNT SCORES FOR MAN UNITED!He takes the ball with a quality turn, and curls it into the corner of the goal 🤩📺 @tntsports & @discoveryplusUK pic.twitter.com/M9ErA2HKbo

Much of the chatter among United fans at present centres on who the third midfield signing will be after Santos and Tielemans.

Given Mount’s injury record, it would be a significant risk not to recruit again in that department in the hope he could stay fit over a full season. Four options in two positions behind the No 10 of Fernandes sounds fine in principle but what happens if Mount’s season was to follow a similar trajectory to the previous three?

If United are going to strengthen in other areas, there will need to be compromises or alternative solutions that help to free up cash along the way but gambling in midfield may not be the best way to go.

With Champions League football to factor in this season, it is still hard to believe United will not seek to strengthen again in midfield but the club seem ready to take their time on that front. And all the while an assortment of names continue to fly around.

After spending £85m on Santos and Tielemans, a massive outlay on a third midfielder at this stage would be a bit of a surprise.

Could that negate a move for Real Madrid’s Aurelien Tchouameni? Alex Scott is greatly admired by United but Bournemouth are determined to keep him and have put a prohibitive pricetag on him.

AS Roma’s Manu Kone is not thought to have universal backing internally. Tyler Adams’ name has been floated again but the Bournemouth and US midfielder’s injury record counts against him.

There has not yet been evidence of a serious appetite to go for Brighton’s Carlos Baleba, whom they considered signing last summer. Sander Berge at Fulham and Borussia Dortmund’s Felix Nmecha are among a number of other midfielders who have been linked with United.

Another midfield signing could well emerge but United are keeping their cards close to their chest. Whatever materialises, though, it will still not change the fact this is a huge season for Mount.

⚽️ Shea Lacey⚽️ Jacob Devaney⚽️ Harry Amass⚽️ Ethan Williams Four #MUAcademy prospects were on the scoresheet in Trondheim 🧬💙 pic.twitter.com/fguQ36ANTM

“It was a good day. Clean sheet, scoring goals and everyone coming through injury-free hopefully is everything you want. Keeping the players fit and improving through pre-season is amongst the most important things. You want to build through the pre-season and you have to manage to players differently. It is never going to be perfect but we scored some great goals and we are moving forward nicely.

“I thought we defended well as a team for the most part. A clean sheet is a beautiful thing. I think we are in a good place with four weeks to go until the start, gradually getting some boys back from the World Cup. As it stands right now, we are in a pretty good place.”

This is what the official start of the season will look like for Michael Carrick’s side:

August 22- Hull vs Manchester UnitedAugust 30- Manchester United vs IpswichSeptember 6- Everton vs Manchester UnitedSeptember 13- Manchester United vs Manchester CitySeptember 20- Fulham vs Manchester United

They face two of the three promoted sides on the first two weekends and there is a very early Manchester derby.

August 1- Manchester United vs Atlético Madrid August 8- PSG vs Manchester United August 12- Manchester United vs Leeds August 15- AC Milan vs Manchester United

Having played Wrexham and Rosenborg in their first two games, the level of competition will rise significantly for Manchester United in the coming weeks.

There is the final whistle and Manchester United have cruised to a 5-0 win over Rosenborg in Norway. Goals from Lacey, Zirkzee, Devaney, Amass and Williams have seen Michael Carrick’s men ease to victory. A pretty one-sided game.

The first yellow card of the game is given very late on as Devaney is booked for a high boot.

A late change for Rosenborg as Hald-Hernes replaces Borgersen.

The visitors have dominated this game and they now have their fifth goal. It is created by great work from Kamason on the right side of the box before he squares it to Williams, who has the easiest of tap-ins at the far post.

Other than a few short periods in this game, Rosenborg have looked poor. They may be midway through their league season but you can see why they are down in 10th in the Norwegian top flight with just four wins from their opening 13 league games.

You would expect that Michael Carrick will be very keen to see his side keep a clean sheet.

Manchester United have their fourth of the evening. Kamason is found making an overlapping run on the right side of the box and his cross fired towards the back post is tapped in by Amass. That was a goal assisted by one full-back and scored by the other.

Good work from Soboczynski results in Rosenborg winning a corner out on the left. They take it short before a shot is hit from the edge of the box straight down the throat of Vitek.

Rosenborg hit the post. Manchester United should probably have been given a free-kick in the build-up as Soboczynski appeared to push Devaney over but play goes on. The ball comes to E Ceide at the far post but his effort strikes the outside of the post.

Just a few minutes after making a raft of changes, Manchester United have their third goal of the evening. Rosenborg fail to clear a corner from the right and the ball falls to Devaney on the six-yard box. He takes one touch before firing into the top of the net.

Bearing in mind Rosenborg are in the middle of their league season, this has been an encouraging showing so far from United. Joshua Zirkzee has been lively. He’s still more likely to leave than stay at Old Trafford this summer but performances like this won’t hamper his value. He set up Shea Lacey for his goal with a good pass after again dropping deep into space and he’s taken that goal to give United a 2-0 lead quite brilliantly. Patrick Dorgu has been a threat and Mason Mount has dovetailed well in central midfield with new signing Andrey Santos.

Both sides are going to make a raft of changes on the hour mark, with the rest of the Manchester United starting XI being changed other than Vitek in goal.

Santos brings down Borgersen not far outside the Manchester United penalty area to give Rosenborg a decent opportunity. It is a pretty decent effort from E Ceide that goes just wide of Vitek’s right post.

The visitors have not been great since the break but they have their second and it is a great solo goal from Zirkzee. Lacey, out on the left touchline, squares it for Zirkzee, who takes the ball towards the Rosenborg penalty area. He fakes a shot, which takes numerous Rosenborg defenders out of the equation as they slide past. He then sits down the Rosenborg keeper before slotting into an empty net. A fine goal from Zirkzee.

Soboczynski has his second chance since coming on at the break after good work from E Ceide down the left but the former’s effort goes wide.

That is a really poor decision from the linesman. Duris was played in behind the Manchester United defence and thought he was through for a one-on-one chance but the offside flag goes up. However, replays prove that Duris was clearly being played onside by Amass, who has looked shaky since coming on at the break.

Zirkzee receives a pass from Dorgu on the D and takes one touch before shooting. His effort takes a deflection and goes behind for a corner, which Wahlstedt slightly unconvincingly punches away.

That is a very good chance for Rosenborg to equalise early in this second half. Amass and Heaven makes a mess of things deep in their own half, presenting Rosenborg with a good opportunity inside the Manchester United penalty area. Two Rosenborg substitutes combine as Soboczynski squares it for Borgersen but the latter makes a mess of it and shoots well wide from 10 yards out.

Michael Carrick has decided to make just a few changes at the break with Amass and Kamason coming on. Shaw and Maguire have gone off, which has seen Yoro move inside from right-back to centre-back.

Our first goalscorer of pre-season = Shea Lacey! 💎 pic.twitter.com/AyFOWNh5Fi

With no delays, the first half is brought to an end and Manchester United take a 1-0 lead into the break courtesy of Lacey’s goal. Expect a raft of chnages at the break.

As this half has worn on, Manchester United’s dominance has only increased.

Mbeumo appeared to be racing through one-on-one but Mortensen just about gets back to outmuscle Mbeumo and allow the ball to go back to his keeper. There were a few appeals for a foul by Mortensen but that challenge was just about fine.

Other than those early stages, Manchester United have dominated the rest of this first half and are pressing for a second. For the second time in the half, they strike the frame of the goal. Mbeumo clips in a cross from the right into the Rosenborg penalty area and it picks out the head of Yoro. However, from eight yards out, the Frenchman’s header comes back off the bar.

Moments after they hit the frame of the goal, Michael Carrick’s side take the lead. Zirkzee picks up the ball inside his own half and, from the halfway line, feeds a pass into the on-running Lacey. Dorgu wants Lacey to play the ball across to him at the back post but the latter opts against it. Instead, just inside the Rosenborg penalty area, he cuts onto his preferred left foot and curls one into the far corner. A good finish from Lacey.

Just as I was saying that both sides were lacking a cutting edge in the final third, Manchester United are inches away from taking the lead as they strike the post. Santos feeds a delicate pass into the path of Dorgu on the left side of the box. Dorgu strikes his effort powerfully but it comes off the outside of the far post.

Both sides have lacked a cutting edge when they get into the opposition final third, hence why there has not been a plethora of good chances.

Mbeumo beats his man down Manchester United’s right and cuts it back to Mount on the edge of the Rosenborg penalty area. Mount hits it first time but his shot is blocked and spins behind for a corner. It is Manchester United’s first of the game but it is headed away.

That was nearly the moment for Rosenborg to take the lead. Pereira’s cross from the left-hand side of the box takes a deflection and nearly ends up at the feet of Chiakha at the back post but it is just out of his reach.

Rosenborg looked the sharper in the early exchanges but Manchester United are growing into the game and starting to gain more control.

Manchester United create their first opening of the game. Rosenborg poorly five the ball away deep inside their half and immediately Zirkzee plays it into the path of Mbeumo, whose shot from the right side of the box is saved by Rosenborg keeper Wahlstedt, who initially spilt the shot but gathered at the second attempt.

Mount trips Sahsah just outside the Manchester United penalty area, which will give Rosenborg a good shot to take an early lead. Rosenborg look a little sharper unsurprisingly in these early stages.

The Rosenborg captain Selnaes takes but hits it straight into the wall.

With Rosenborg in the midst of their season and Manchester United just in their second pre-season game, you would expect the hosts to have more rhythm and flow in their game.

Manchester United to appear to be lining up with a back four, with Yoro starting at right-back rather than his more customary centre-back position.

We are under way in Norway. Rosenborg are playing in white, with Manchester United in blue.

Both sides emerge from the tunnel, with Harry Maguire leading Manchester United out, and we are getting closer to kick-off in Norway.

Rosenborg: Wahlstedt, Mortensen, Singsdal Volden, Nemcik, Pereira; Bomholt, Selnaes, Fossum, Sunde, Chiakha, Sahsah.Substitutes: Sandberg, Amdam, M. Ceide, Rosten, Witry, Dahl, Hald-Hernes, Slordal, Hedman, Borgersen, Bakke, E. Ceide, Duris, Soboczynski.

Manchester United: Vitek; Yoro, Maguire, Heaven, Shaw; Santos, Mount; Lacey, Zirkzee, Dorgu; Mbeumo.Substitutes: Heaton, Mee, Amass, Armer, Kamason, Collyer, Devaney, J. Fletcher, T. Fletcher, Gore, Thwaites, Gabriel, Obi, Williams.

It’s a good opportunity for Shea Lacey tonight. He’s expected to be deployed in the hole in behind Joshua Zirkzee. A talented, highly technical footballer with a good left foot, he’ll be wanting to make the most of the chance. Another opportunity for Mason Mount to stake a claim in one of the two deeper midfield positions next to new signing Andrey Santos. Big season ahead for Mount.

INS:Andrey Santos ⇠ Chelsea, £48mYouri Tielemans ⇠ Aston Villa, £36mKarl Darlow ⇠ Leeds, FreeTynan Thompson ⇠ Tottenham, £4m

OUTS:Casemiro ⇢ Inter Miami, FreeRasmus Hojlund ⇢ Napoli, £38mJadon Sancho, FreeTyrell Malacia, Free

Forward JJ Gabriel, who does not turn 16 until October, is on the bench for Manchester United this evening. The 15-year-old has represented England at U15, U16 and U17 level. He won the inaugural Premier League Under-18 Player of the Season award for the 2025/26 campaign.

Starting XI: Vitek; Yoro, Maguire (captain), Heaven, Shaw; Santos, Mount; Lacey, Zirkzee, Dorgu; Mbeumo.Substitutes: Heaton, Mee, Amass, Armer, Kamason, Collyer, Devaney, J.Fletcher, T.Fletcher, Gore, Thwaites, Gabriel, Obi, Williams.

Dagens 11 utvalgte 🖤🤍Avspark er klokken 18.00 🏟️ pic.twitter.com/LuZrojJM4l

Bring on United! 🫡Watch Rosenborg v United LIVE on MUTV, with build-up starting at 16:00 BST 📲

Manchester United’s preparations for the new season continue in Norway as they take on Rosenborg in their second pre-season game. These sides did meet in a pre-season friendly two years ago in July 2024, with Rosenborg winning that encounter 1-0.

Manchester United kicked off their pre-season against Wrexham nearly a week ago, which they lost 1-0 in Helsinki. Michael Carrick opted to deploy two different XIs for each half, meaning 22 players got a run-out. Manchester United kick off their Premier League campaign at newly promoted Hull City on August 22.

They have added two midfielders to their ranks over the last few weeks, both from the Premier League. Brazilian Andrey Santos has joined from Chelsea whilst Belgium’s Youri Tielemans has arrived from Aston Villa. Santos made his first Manchester United appearance in the loss to Wrexham whilst Tielemans is yet to feature having made the knockout stages with Belgium at the World Cup. A number of players are still yet to return from World Cup duty, including the likes of Lisandro Martinez, Marcus Rashford and Kobbie Mainoo, although Rashford still faces an uncertain future.

Former Leeds goalkeeper Karl Darlow has also arrived but he is currently recovering from a minor procedure. Benjamin Sesko is still trying to shake off a shin injury whilst Matthijs de Ligt is not yet available due to a back injury which plagued for most of last season. Manuel Ugarte faces a lengthy spell on the sidelines having picked up a serious injury whilst playing for Uruguay at the World Cup. After this game, the level of competition for Manchester United for the rest of pre-season ramps up a number of notches, with the likes of Atlético Madrid and back-to-back European champions PSG to come over the next couple of weeks as Carrick’s men prepare for a season in which they return to the Champions League.

Rosenborg are in the midst of their league campaign in Norway and are experiencing a tricky campaign. They are currently 10th in the Norwegian top flight, having won just four of their 13 league games thus far, but their form has picked up of late as they have won three of their last five games. They won their last match 3-0 against Start six days ago.

#1931. Juventus have £87m budget and five strikers on their radar, including two from the Premier League

By Axel Clody | 05 Nov 2026 11:33

Juventus have a budget of around £85m (€100m) to invest in the transfer market. The club are looking at the striker market with five names in mind.

On Tuesday, the Juventus shareholders’ meeting was held to approve the club’s accounts. The £212.5m (€250m) capital increase aims to ‘strengthen the capital structure and sporting competitiveness, to fund possible improvements to strategic real estate assets (mainly the Allianz Stadium), to enhance the brand and to ensure the economic and financial viability of the club’.

In this respect, CalcioMercato reports that the capital increase could allow Juventus to have a budget of around £85m (€100m) to invest in the market, from the winter window through to next summer. It is a substantial sum with which to sign high-level players.

Given the difficulties encountered by Luciano Spalletti’s side at the start of the season, investment as early as the next winter window cannot be ruled out.

Signing a striker appears to be Juventus’ priority, as Randal Kolo Muani and Nick Woltemade are not delivering: they have scored only one goal between them in ten Serie A matchdays.

Spalletti is looking for a forward with a profile similar to that of Dusan Vlahovic, who left last summer, and who is capable of being particularly effective in front of goal. The Italian outlet reveals the existence of a shortlist of five strikers on Juventus’ radar.

Benjamin Sesko and Folarin Balogun are high on the list and will be monitored closely by Juventus over the coming weeks.

The American is one of the five players most likely to leave Monaco, while the Slovenian, who is currently injured with a shin problem, is struggling to live up to the £65m (€76.5m) Manchester United invested to sign him in the summer of 2025.

Brian Brobbey is also on this Turin shortlist, but the Dutch forward is unlikely to leave Sunderland this winter, as he has just extended his contract until June 2031. Juventus are also interested in two young forwards in great form: Antonio Raimondo and Younes Ebnoutalib.

The 22-year-old Italian striker has scored eight goals in nine league matches for Frosinone, but he injured an ankle last weekend. A winter move therefore looks unlikely, as he is not expected to return to action before 2027. Ebnoutalib, a 23-year-old German striker, is also in sparkling form for Eintracht Frankfurt, with eight goals in ten matches this season.

#1930. Tuttosport: Foster could follow Battersea Power Station lead to preserve San Siro – the idea

It is possible that the plans for the existing San Siro – once the new stadium is constructed – could change slightly.

Milan and Inter unveiled the Generali Stadium last Thursday, which will be the new 71,500-seat stadium for the two clubs, but the future of their current home is still uncertain according to Tuttosport (via MilanPress).

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The idea was to demolish a large part of the San Siro, keeping standing only a south-east portion, around 30% of the external ramps. A piece of the Curva Sud would be preserved and a part of the orange stand, areas that will be used for new purposes.

Some politicians – especially Senate President Ignazio La Russa – have always maintained that demolition isn’t necessary even with the new stadium. This concept has never been discussed by the two clubs or the council, but it could serve as an example to follow.

The paper adds that Norman Foster – one of the design architects behind the Generali Stadium – has declared that he wants to preserve a larger part of San Siro. It could follow the route of one of the previous projects in which he took part at Battersea Power Station in London.

The building was restored by WilkinsonEye, but Foster’s studio played a key role in the area redevelopment with the Battersea Roof Gardens and 50 Electric Boulevard.

Battersea has thus remained a hub in London with a shopping centre inside and a whole neighbourhood around it on the river front, a move that could perhaps also be applied to the Meazza.

#1929. The turning point that inspired Celtic to big European victory against Besiktas

On Guy Fawkes night, Celtic finally provided some European fireworks. Martin O'Neill's side got their Europa League campaign up and running with an enthralling 3-2 win over Besiktas.

Junior Olaitain put the visitors ahead in the 54th minute, scoring from the rebound of his own penalty kick that was initially saved by Sam Johnstone.

Celtic Park was engulfed by an all too familiar feeling before O'Neill introduced Callum Osmand and Camilo Duran in the 60th minute.

Osmand scored the equaliser seconds after coming on, with Duran latching on to the youngster's through ball to round Alex Nubel and put Celtic ahead with 12 minutes remaining.

Orkun Kokcu's pile-driver levelled things up for less than 120 seconds as Duran struck again in the 88th minute to give Celtic a priceless victory.

Here are the key talking points from Parkhead...

Celtic's Callum Osmand scored against Besiktas. (Image: Andrew Milligan/PA)

O’Neill made five changes from Sunday’s defeat at Falkirk, most notably drafting Jordan Lotomba in for his first start at right-back.

The Switzerland international had played just 31 minutes in green-and-white hoops before Besiktas, making his inclusion all the more surprising.

Lotomba was tasked with keeping Besiktas' left side quiet though former Arsenal attacker Leandro Trossard and Ernest Poku kept him well occupied.

The 28-year-old sought to maraud forward when he could, but once tripped up on his own feet when attempting a series of step-overs in the opposition third.

The concession of a second-half penalty compounded Lotomba's tough evening. He was withdrawn in the 60th minute for Colby Donovan.

Elsewhere, Kasper Hogh, James Forrest, and Sebastian Tounekti made up a second string frontline.

Duran, Celtic’s top scorer this season, dropped to the bench along with Haissem Hassan. But it wasn’t a completely rotated XI.

Regulars Kieran Tierney, Cameron Carter-Vickers, Liam Scales, and captain Callum McGregor all began, with Benjamin Nygren and Mika Baur also in from the off.

That said, it was the first time O’Neill hadn’t gone full strength in Europe this season, perhaps indicating his feelings at Celtic’s current plight.

There are dull halves of football, and then there are dull halves of football. Besiktas enjoyed the majority of possession (61 per cent) in the opening 45 minutes without mustering many opportunities.

Celtic's sound structure limited the visitors' attacking play. Carter-Vickers defended ably but O'Neill's side struggled to get forward themselves.

By the break, Celtic had just one shot on goal, two touches in the opposition box, and 73 per cent pass accuracy, compared to around 88 per cent in their first three Europa League defeats.

Yet again, their inability to progress play through the lines was apparent. Celtic resorted to going long on a number of occasions. Hogh failed to make it stick and Tounekti struggled greatly.

Besiktas were quite content to pop the ball around, without taking any major risks. You still felt the Turks had a few more gears to move through.

Celtic shouldn't have needed a second-half wake-up call but just seconds after the interval, Trossard fired just shy of the left post.

Moments later, Johnstone's clearance ricocheted off the Belgian attacker and into Lotomba's right-back area. The Celtic defender slid needlessly in on Poku and referee Sascha Stegemann pointed to the spot without hesitation.

Olaitan stepped up and Johnstone made a heroic save that flew into the smoke-filled Glasgow sky, only for the initial taker to score on the rebound.

Just like Johnstone, Lotomba almost redeemed himself in the following seconds, driving forward from his defensive position before tumbling over the ball when attempting to shoot.

But Besiktas weren't ahead for long. O'Neill looked to his bench for fresh impetus on the hour mark and within just a minute of coming on, Osmand scored.

McGregor latched brilliantly on to a loose midfield pass and cut back for the substitute, who scored with practically his first touch.

Celtic Park had all of a sudden rediscovered its European voice.

For the goal, McGregor looked like his old self, driving forward from the engine room to kickstart a promising attack and Osmand provided the killer touch with his first European goal.

If O'Neill's plan was to wait until the game opened up in the second half and then call on the cavalry, it worked a treat.

Just 16 minutes after Osmand drew Celtic level with a fine strike of his own, he turned provider, playing a slide-rule pass in behind Besiktas' defence for Duran.

The Colombian got there ahead of Nubel and slotted beyond the goal line to turn the game on its head.

Duran didn't have to wait long to make his presence felt again, once more beating Nubel, this time from close range, after brilliantly controlling Tierney's mishit shot. It came seconds after Kokcu's leveller.

A true difference-maker, Duran is now up to 13 goals for the season. His impact could not have been greater here.

Well, who saw that coming? After four matchdays, Celtic are finally up and running in the Europa League. It really was now or never for O'Neill's charges, who have given their chances of progression to the knockout stages fresh hope with an unlikely victory.

Beyond their run of six defeats in ten leading into Thursday night, what made the win even more unexpected was the fact Besiktas are the best side they've played at home in the league phase so far.

Celtic struggled greatly against both Ferencvaros and Celta Vigo on their own turf, flailing whenever faced with adversity. They went down meekly in Lisbon too, losing 4-1 to Benfica last month.

No one should get carried away based on one result. Celtic still need somewhere in the region of six to eight points to finish in the top 24 and three out of their four remaining fixtures are away.

The next comes in Leiria against Portuguese second tier side Torreense after the international break. They could realistically gain three more points there before a trip to face Omonia Nicosia in December. Ties against Marseille and Union St-Gilloise lie ahead in January.

O'Neill will take great satisfaction from a European result that's long evaded his team. Time will define its influence on Celtic's wider Europa League picture.

#1928. Cristiano Ronaldo: Portugal icon releases video statement confirming international retirement

By Oliver Thomas | 05 Nov 2026 11:41, Last updated: 05 Nov 2026 11:47

Portugal icon Cristiano Ronaldo has officially announced his retirement from international football.

Widely regarded as one of, if not the, greatest player of all time, the 41-year-old has decided to call time on his legendary 23-year career with Portugal.

Ronaldo holds the record for the most international caps (234), most international goals (146) and most international victories (141) in the men’s game, while he has also won Euro 2016 and two Nations League titles with Portugal.

The five-time Ballon d'Or winner's decision to bring the curtain down on his glittering international career comes after a fall-out with head coach Jorge Jesus during the September/October international break.

Ronaldo was handed a 30-day suspension and €255 fine by the Portuguese FA after he walked out of the Portugal camp last month after being told he would not start a UEFA Nations League match against Denmark.

Jesus refused to close the door on bringing Ronaldo back into the first-team fold for November’s break, but the Al-Nassr star has taken to social media to end his Portugal career once and for all.

Ronaldo’s decision to retire from Portugal duty comes just a month after long-term rival Lionel Messi played his 208th and final game for Argentina.

A post shared by Cristiano Ronaldo (@cristiano)

In a video posted on Instagram, Ronaldo said: “The day has come back for me to hand back the number 7 shirt of our national team.

“I never felt it belonged to me alone, but for 23 years I had the privilege and the responsibility of wearing it, defending it, and carrying it with me into stadiums all around the world.

“Today, the time has come to pass it on to the future. It was not an easy decision, because some decisions are not made with the mind alone. They are also made with the heart.

“A journey that began in August 2003 and changed my life forever has come to an end. When I look back at everything with the national team, I don’t just see the matches, goals, records or trophies.

“I see people. I see the Portuguese people living abroad who, for 90 minutes, felt a little closer to home. I see millions of Portuguese people I have never met but who became part of my life.

“Because at the end of the day, football is so much bigger than a game. Football is about people.

"I spent my life working to be the best player in the world. Today I realise that the greatest victory was to have deserved to represent the best country in the world."

Ronaldo thanked his teammates, coaches, family and supporters from around the world, adding: "Thank you for these 23 years. Thank you for having believed in me. Portugal will always be in me. Forever."

Meanwhile, a statement from the Portuguese Football Federation expressed “deep gratitude and immense admiration” for Ronaldo’s service to the country.

“Cristiano Ronaldo has raised Portugal’s profile and inspired generations of young people who dream of following in his footsteps; for many of us, he is the greatest player of all time!” the federation said.

They have also stated that they intends to organise a tribute to Ronaldo “in which the fans and the country can one more time applaud and celebrate a player who has given us so much”.

Ronaldo’s decision to retire from Portugal duty means that he will miss November’s international fixtures against Denmark and Wales.

His 234th and final game for his country was a 1-0 victory against Wales in the Nations League in September, while his final goal was scored from the penalty spot against Croatia (2-1 win) in July during the 2026 World Cup.

Ronaldo will now focus on his club career with Saudi Pro League side Al-Nassr as he continues to chase down 1,000 career goals – he currently sits on 985 goals in all competitions.

CR7 has previously stated that “this is probably my last year of football, and I want to leave a spectacular legacy”, with retirement from all football a genuine possibility in 2027.

#1927. Wouter Vrancken demands unity as Hearts seek to bounce back from Thun defeat

Wouter Vrancken insists Hearts will have to stick together following their self-inflicted 3-1 Conference League defeat by Thun in Switzerland.

The Scottish outfit, without 10 players through various injuries, fell behind in the 22nd minute when defender Jamie McCart knocked the ball into his own net.

Thun doubled their lead in the 33rd minute through striker Brighton Labeau after a poor attempted clearance from captain Stephen Kingsley – who went off later with an injury – and then Furkan Dursun grabbed a third in the 56th minute.

Jambos defender Stuart Findlay then gave some unrealised hope of a comeback in the 82nd minute when he headed in from close range.

After three Conference League fixtures Hearts have one point out of nine and have won just two of their last 10 fixtures in all competitions.

Vrancken told TNT Sports: “Like I said already to the guys, we have to stick together now.

“We know which situation we’re in with all the circumstances.

“And there’s only one thing that you have to do now and that is stick together and keep working hard.

“In general, it was not good enough in quality and can you blame them?

“Yeah, on one hand you can because you want to always expect the best and want the best.

“On the other hand, I’m still proud of what they did already in the run-up games.”

Kingsley was replaced in the second half by 19-year-old Matthew Gillies, called back from a loan spell at Stenhousemuir amid the club’s injury crisis, and Vrancken admitted there was an element of risk playing him on the artificial surface which the Jambos boss had criticised.

He said: “We talked it through before the game of course, a few days before the game.

“And yeah, it’s always a risk, especially when it’s another surface, and especially when it’s bad like that, but he was confident in playing and that’s where we are.”

Hearts’ next Conference League game is against Ligue 1 side in Monaco at Tynecastle on November 26 but Vrancken is more concerned about the home William Hill Premiership game against Falkirk on Sunday.

He said: “Monaco’s a really strong side, maybe the strongest side we will face in Europe.

#1926. Arsenal vs. Hull City: Head-to-head record and past meetings

By Ben Knapton | 05 Nov 2026 11:53

Premier League ever-presents Arsenal and top-flight returnees Hull City clash at the Emirates Stadium in Saturday's gameweek 10 encounter.

The Gunners will temporarily go six points clear at the top of the Premier League table with victory over their newly-promoted foes, having moved three above Manchester City in last weekend's 1-0 success at Liverpool.

Meanwhile, Sergej Jakirovic's Hull will break into the top 10 of the rankings with all three points, but they have failed to win any of their last eight games across all tournaments.

Here, Sports Mole takes an in-depth look at the head-to-head record and previous meetings between the two sides.

Arsenal vs. Hull City has been a collector's item on the English football calendar, compared to some of the most common matchups in the land, as the two clubs have only met on 26 occasions in all competitions.

Unsurprisingly, the head-to-head dominance belongs to the Gunners, who have beaten the Tigers 18 times while suffering just three defeats and settling for a point on five occasions.

Arsenal actually failed to win any of their first three battles with Hull, playing out two draws and suffering one loss between 1908 and 1913 as Woolwich Arsenal, and they only earned two victories from their first seven head-to-heads.

However, the reigning Premier League champions have since triumphed in 16 of their last 19 contests, most notably the 2013-14 FA Cup final, when Arsene Wenger's men fell 2-0 down inside just eight minutes but magnificently fought back to prevail 3-2 and end their nine-year trophy drought.

The Gunners have also avoided defeat in each of their last 14 clashes with the Tigers, although Hull's last win in this particular fixture was a momentous one, as a Geovanni-inspired side shocked the Emirates with a 2-1 success in 2008, shortly after their maiden ascent to the top flight.

Arsenal responded to that harrowing evening with a seven-match winning run against Hull, and their current victorious sequence now stands at three games, including a Premier League double in 2016-17.

Alexis Sanchez was Hull's nemesis that year, scoring twice in a 4-1 away win before bagging another brace in a 2-0 home victory, and the Chilean is the highest documented scorer in this fixture with eight in total.

Nicklas Bendtner, Theo Walcott and Aaron Ramsey each scored three against the Tigers, meanwhile, the latter memorably snatching 2014 FA Cup glory for Arsenal in extra time.

#1925. GdS: Milan enjoying the ‘best ever’ version of Rabiot – renewal imminent as figures emerge

Adrien Rabiot continues to dazzle with his performances and goal contributions, which AC Milan intend to reward him for.

La Gazzetta dello Sport confirm that the discussions between Rabiot and Milan have been underway for some time regarding an ‘update’ to the terms of his contract. Gerry Cardinale has very clear ideas about his priorities, and the Frenchman is next on the list.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

In recent months, several players have ascended to the fourth floor of Casa Milan to sign extensions. There have been the young talents (Camarda and Comotto, 2031), veterans (Modric, 2027) and core pieces within the squad (Pavlovic, Pulisic, 2031).

Rabiot clearly belongs to the latter category (but also to a certain extent the same one as Modric) and has become the most urgent task to complete in terms of contracts.

The parties are in fact talking based on a shared desire to move forward together. For Cardinale, Rabiot represents one of the pillars on which the team’s rebuilding will continue.

Rabiot is seen as a player with the wisdom of experience, a perfect example for the younger players, and someone with the qualities of a leader even without the captain’s armband. Milan want to get back to the top, by Cardinale’s admission, and they need players like Adrien to help the cause.

So, a contract extension until 2030 has been ready for him for some time now (his current one expires in 2028). After the summer Napoli rumours, Rabiot remained at Milan partly because of his existing deal, but also partly because Cardinale convinced him.

What happens now? The next crucial step will be with his mother. Indeed, it is Mrs. Véronique who manages the former PSG midfielder’s interests, and a meeting will take place shortly. A pay rise from €3.5m net per season to €5m per year – what Pulisic earns – seems reasonable to presume.

With Rabiot on nine goal contributions for the season (five goals, four assists) he needs just one more to match his total from the entirety of 2025-26. So, he seems to be ageing like a fine French wine. All that’s needed is a final push on the contract front to continue an undoubtedly happy marriage.

#1922. Harry Kane: Record-breaking Bayern Munich contract confirmed as Ballon d’Or winner surpasses Kylian Mbappe’s salary

By Oliver Thomas | 05 Nov 2026 11:55

Bayern Munich have announced that 2026 Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane has committed his future to the club by signing a new contract until June 2029.

The 33-year-old striker was approaching the final six months of his pre-existing deal, with La Liga champions Barcelona believed to have been keeping tabs on his situation.

Despite a lengthy negotiation process, Kane was determined to continue his career with Bayern where he has scored a staggering 156 goals in 161 games since joining from Tottenham Hotspur three years ago.

According to multiple reports, including The Athletic, Kane’s new deal is the most lucrative in Bayern’s history, with the striker now said to be the highest-paid player in Europe by salary.

In comparison, Manchester City’s Erling Haaland became the highest-paid Premier League player in January 2025 when he agreed a £500,000-per-week contract until the summer of 2034.

Kylian Mbappe, meanwhile, is thought to be pocketing around £518,000 a week at Real Madrid, but Kane is now believed to be earning more than both strikers.

It is also claimed that Bayern do not view this significant contract as Kane’s last agreement with the club, as their clear desire is to retain his invaluable services well into the future.

“I feel right at home at FC Bayern. I love the club, the fans and the city of Munich,” Kane told the club’s official website after signing his new deal.

“We have a fantastic team and, in Vincent Kompany, a fantastic manager. It makes me very proud to be part of this club. My whole family is very happy here.

“I was keen to stay. I’m now looking forward to the future and I want to win many more titles with this great club.”

Herbert Hainer, Bayern’s club president, added: “What began as a major transfer has, over time, become a special chapter in FC Bayern’s history.

“Harry Kane lives up to every promise football has to offer, and he has secured his place in the hearts of the fans as one of the greatest figures in the sport of our time.

“My compliments to Jan-Christian Dreesen and our sporting management team. This is a special moment for FC Bayern today.”

CEO Dreesen continued: “We’re delighted to have successfully extended Harry Kane’s contract. This is fantastic news for us, for our fans and for the Bundesliga.

“The Ballon d’Or winner is staying at Bayern Munich! Since joining us in 2023, he has achieved extraordinary things with his goals, his influence on the game and as a role model both on and off the pitch.

“He has long since made FC Bayern his home, has continued to develop with us and crowned that development with the Ballon d’Or. His contract extension is a commitment to FC Bayern and to a story that is far from over.”

Bayern board member for sport Max Eberl, who has regularly provided updates on Kane’s future in the media, added: “This key contract extension gives us certainty in our planning. It sends a message that the biggest goals are within reach at FC Bayern.

“Players like Harry Kane offer a team unique opportunities. We’re delighted that he will continue to be a key figure who helps shape the direction of the club, and with whom we can continue to build our squad for the future.”

Kane is hoping to win a third consecutive Bundesliga title with Bayern this season as well as fire the German giants to their first Champions League trophy since 2020.

#1920. Guimaraes will not force Newcastle exit like Isak, says Howe

Eddie Howe is confident Bruno Guimarães will not demand to leave Newcastle United for Arsenal and echo Alexander Isak’s acrimonious departure to Liverpool last summer.

Howe admitted he could not guarantee that Guimarães will still be at the club in September but gave a strong defence of his captain’s character and insisted the Brazil international will return for pre-season training next week as planned.

Given the huge gap between Newcastle’s valuation of Guimarães and what Arsenal have indicated they would be willing to pay for the 28-year-old, there is a belief on Tyneside that the only way the captain would join the London club is if he behaved as badly as Isak did 12 months ago.

Newcastle value Guimarães at £100m, while Arsenal, through intermediaries, have only indicated they would be willing to pay about £60m including bonuses.

Isak did not travel on the club’s pre-season tour to Asia and then went on strike, refusing to train or play, until Newcastle agreed to sell him to Liverpool for a British record £128m on deadline day.

Asked if he feared a repeat of that with Guimarães this time around, Howe replied: “I’ve spoken to him as I would do with Bruno normally. He is a fantastic person and we have had some really good conversations both before, during and after the World Cup. What we speak about obviously has to remain private but he is a great player and a great person.

“Look, I don’t know what is going to happen with Bruno. That is up to other people to speculate about but also other people to have conversations about which I’m not a part of. I don’t think it is fair to compare situations and what happened previously. You’ve got to look at this in its own right.

“Bruno is captain of our football club. He has been an unbelievable player and person all the time we have worked together. I speak on behalf of everyone at the football club when I say we absolutely love him and of course everyone wants him to stay.

“The plan is for him to come back on July 31, he gets an extended break because of the World Cup and is currently enjoying a holiday with his family... There is nothing to say that Bruno won’t be back training with us.”

"We've had some really good conversations" 🗣️Eddie Howe speaks on Newcastle's transfer window so far and speculation around Bruno Guimarães ⚫️⚪️ pic.twitter.com/zB1W31Fne0

Arsenal’s interest in Guimarães is well known but there has been little progress since they began their pursuit more than a month ago.

Whether Arsenal can come up with an offer that tempts Newcastle into negotiations remains to be seen but it is thought the Premier League champions will try to harden up their interest before Guimarães returns for pre-season training.

Newcastle United were held to a 1-1 draw by Gateshead in their second pre-season friendly of the summer. A 79th-minute own-goal saved the Premier League club’s blushes but what did we learn from the match?

Steur did not grab many headlines when he arrived from Ajax for £20m earlier this month because of Sandro Tonali’s move to Tottenham Hotspur. But those familiar with Dutch football would have been excited that Newcastle had signed him.

The 18-year-old has impressed with his performances in training and gave a glimpse of his significant potential in his first public display. He is young and sources have told Telegraph Sport that he must develop physically before he is ready to play every week in the Premier League – but you can already see he has a very high ceiling.

As you would expect from a player described as Ajax’s best midfield prospect for a generation, he is assured on the ball. He is also a progressive passer, always looking to break the lines to get his team moving forward. Eddie Howe will love him.

Whisper it, but there were shades of Bruno Guimarães in his style of play, in the way he took the ball under pressure, in tight spaces, and played on the turn. Patience will be needed but the signs are really encouraging.

Guimarães’s future is all supporters have wanted to speak about for weeks. I was at a wedding on Friday and it felt like everyone asked me about it at some point – including the bride and groom immediately after completing their first dance.

It has already become a summer-long transfer saga that has not progressed since Arsenal’s interest was revealed last month. Telegraph Sport has repeatedly checked whether there have been any fresh developments over the past week and the answer from senior Newcastle sources has remained consistent: there are no talks ongoing and nothing has accelerated, despite claims Arsenal were preparing an official £70m bid.

However, Newcastle need clarity from their captain. He is due back for pre-season next week and is expected to fly to Spain for their training camp on July 31. He has intimated he would like to move to Arsenal but unless Newcastle receive a bid that matches their asking price, he and his representatives have been told he will not be allowed to leave.

Schär has been a brilliant player for Newcastle, but at the age of 34 and coming off the back of a serious ankle injury, he looked understandably rusty against Gateshead.

This will be the former Switzerland international’s ninth season at St James’ Park and he was at fault for giving away a soft free-kick that led to Gateshead scoring first.

Schar accepted a contract extension earlier this summer on reduced terms and although Howe values his quality and experience, he is going to be a back-up centre-back this season.

Neave, 19, started the game as Newcastle’s centre-forward as Will Osula was missing and Nick Woltemade and Yoane Wissa were given additional time off after playing in the World Cup for Germany and DR Congo respectively.

But those players will return to training next week and, although Neave forced a good save in the first half, he is not ready to start in the Premier League. There is little point keeping him around as a fourth-choice striker when he needs to be playing regularly at this stage of his career.

A loan move is on the cards and he could be a really smart signing for a Championship club or a team competing at the top of League One. The most important thing is that he gets regular senior games rather than hangs around at Newcastle on the fringes of the first-team squad.

Eddie Howe has said "he does not know" what will happen with Bruno but pretty strong defence of his character and denied similarities with Isak. Said they have spoken regularly throughout the summer and he will be back for pre season training on July 31st #nufc

Eddie Howe’s side will head down to Ashton Gate before jetting off to La Manga for a training camp on July 31, which will feature many of those who played in the World Cup, including Bruno Guimarães who has been linked with a move to Arsenal.

In Spain, Newcastle will face Valencia at the Mestalla, before returning to the UK to play Everton at Murrayfield. They will then host Bayer Leverkusen and Strasbourg at St James’ Park for their final tune-up matches before the Premier League season starts.

Neave comes close to opening the scoring, firing an effort across the face of goal that goes behind for a corner.

Hall then gets a shot away from the edge of the box, but cannot keep his half-volley down and the ball sails over the bar.

Newcastle look most dangerous when Schar steps up and punches in those line-breaking passes. Gateshead defending resolutely, though, keeping things compact across the backline.

Murphy earns his side a free-kick down the right. He delivers the ball himself, with the box loaded with Schar and Murphy, and the former steals in to the near post but cannot quite stoop down low enough to get a meaningful contact on the ball. Desbois gathers without fuss.

Newcastle have won a glut of corners down their left, all of which have been taken short. The latest is played out to Steur who rains in a cross which is claimed by the goalkeeper.

Sean Steur looks like a player... some really nice touches from the young Dutchman. He is always looking to make a progressive pass and has been a real bright spark. Newcastle have dominated the game. As you would expect against opposition four divisions below them

Another tidy involvement from Steur, who disguises a pass to Ramsey on the edge of the box. The ball is worked into the path of Murphy and deflects out for a corner. The former Ajax midfielder is growing in confidence.

Hall puts in another ball from the left, this time to the back post, where the ball is headed away by Ferguson.

New signing Steur is starting to creep forward, carrying the ball nicely and picking it back up in the right channel. He stands a cross up to the near post but Murphy’s header is dealt with by Desbois.

Hall works a yard of space in a dangerous area down the left moments later, but the ball ricochets back off him and out for goal-kick.

Hall punches in a lovely ball down the line for Barnes to run on to, but the move is snuffed out by Robinson.

It does seem strange that this game has not sold out. There are thought to be about 7,000 fans inside the stadium, which once had a capacity of more than 11,000 when it was one of the country’s premier athletics venues. They even used to have Diamond League events here not so long ago.

But the capacity has been steadily reduced for safety reasons and it is rarely used for anything other than local athletic events and Gateshead FC games.

There were officially only 50 tickets left for sale a few minutes before kick-off, but there are lots of empty seats.

Chadwick lofts a tidy cross in from the left, but Boatswain’s header drifts wide of the mark. The chance came off a decent spell of possession from Cattermole’s side, the most fluent they have been in this match so far.

Ramsey regains possession high up the pitch and releases Barnes who plays in Murphy, but the Newcastle forward mistimes his run and the linesman’s flag goes up. A promising counter.

Ramsey is brought down on the edge of the box as he tries to break free and the referee awards a free-kick. There are a few contenders to take it (Schar, Barnes, Hall) but in the end it is Barnes who gets a shot away, but his curled effort flies just wide of the mark.

Another weighted ball over the top from Schar puts Anifowose under pressure in the left channel but his ball across the face of goal is cleared to safety by a team-mate.

Newcastle circulating the ball in front of Gateshead’s first line of pressure. The hosts regain possession but struggle to find a way through Newcastle’s midfield.

Schar getting a few early touches as he makes his return from injury. He plays a long, raking diagonal out to Barnes who cannot quite get past his man.

Neave tests Desbois with a well-struck effort off the next phase of play.

The officials and both sets of players line up behind a banner with the message ‘Rest in peace, Kevin Keegan’. Newcastle are in their new navy-blue away shirt, with Gateshead in their home white-and-black kit. A minute’s silence is then observed immaculately.

The tributes left in honour of Kevin Keegan outside St James’ Park is a sight to behold, with flowers, shirts and scarves covering the ground and steps in the south-west corner. It is a very moving thing to behold as people come to pay their respects to the Newcastle legend.

There will also be a minute’s silence before today’s game against Gateshead.

Some time tidy centre-forward play from Levi Amantchi in last week’s 3-3 draw. The target man has since been loaned to Kidderminster Harriers...

A post shared by Gateshead FC (@gfc_official)

Incomings Bazoumana Touré ⇠ Hoffenheim, £43mAladji Bamba ⇠ Monaco, £30mSean Steur ⇠ Ajax, £20mEwen Jaouen ⇠ Stade Reims, £18m

OutgoingsSandro Tonali ⇢ Tottenham Hotspur, £92.5mAnthony Gordon ⇢ Barcelona, £68mKieran Trippier ⇢ Wolverhampton Wanderers, FreeMatt Targett ⇢ Hull City, FreeEmil Krafth, FreeJohn Ruddy, Free

It has been a difficult and, at times, acrimonious 12 months for Eddie Howe, who must have wondered whether the job was still worth the hassle given the criticism and online vitriol he received at times last season.

Few would have blamed him if he had quit, but Howe has always been fully committed and always knew there would be a period like this to come through.

He has been in the job almost five years and last season was the first time he had been vilified by a section of the fanbase. It left its mark. The boos that followed defeats at St James’ Park hurt and he worried the unity that had powered the team’s success had fractured irreparably.

The apparent collective shrug that greeted another run to the Carabao Cup semi-final, while guiding the team into the knockout rounds of the Champions League for the first time was a source of bewilderment and frustration.

Howe has not complained or moaned. Although he wobbled towards the end of last season and there were some calling for him to be sacked, he was supported and encouraged by those above him. That loyalty mattered.

The problem is, negativity lingers in the fanbase. Even a picture of Howe at pre-season training, posted on social media by the club, led to abusive comments questioning his ability and character. Some of it was toxic. It was rightly called out by other supporters.

Goals from Elliot Anderson (wonder what happened to him?!), Allan Saint-Maximin and Jay Turner-Cooke helped Newcastle overturn a 2-0 half-time deficit when they last visited Gateshead International Stadium in 2023.

Speaking through Gateshead’s club media, Cattermole said of facing Newcastle: “It’s obviously a different test. We have to respect the opposition, they’re a high-quality team and it might not be what we’re getting in our league but we’ll still try to implement what we believe we want to be in and out of possession. It’ll be a great physical challenge for us.

He added: “They [my players] have all shown up great. What a game for them. What a game for them to go and test yourself against some big names and fantastic coaching staff, for us all it’s a great challenge for us. We hope we give them a good test, we hope we give them the challenge they want as well. I played in many of these games as a player as well. We expect it to be competitive.”

💬 "What a game for [the players] to go & play."Lee Cattermole talks tomorrow's game against @NUFC at the GIS ⤵️📺👉 https://t.co/DGuJRosJ2K pic.twitter.com/rccs5FzhG6

A classic first-game-of-pre-season vibe to Newcastle’s team sheet as established stars rub shoulders with youngsters from the academy.

Only one of their four summer signings, former Ajax midfielder Sean Steur, starts the game and there will be a lot of interest in the 18-year-old. The youngster has impressed in training over the last couple of weeks but it is thought he has a lot of work to do physically to be ready for the Premier League.

Full-back Leo Shahar was in and around the first team last season as was striker Sean Neave. Alex Murphy, who started one game in the Champions League last season is expected to go out on loan before the window shuts, but starts alongside Fabian Schar in the centre of defence.

Worryingly there is no sign of Sven Botman and Will Osula who both played in the behind-closed-doors friendly against Darlington last weekend.

Joelinton, Tino Livramento and Lewis Miley are still being eased back into things after injuries at the end of last season.

Another new signing, goalkeeper Ewen Jaouen, is on the bench and will play the second half against their National League neighbours.

Gateshead lost manager Rob Elliot to Carlisle at the end of last season and are now managed by former Sunderland and Middlesbrough midfielder Lee Cattermole.

Arrivals in Gateshead 👋 pic.twitter.com/9hTtruxGEo

Fabian Schär returns from an ankle injury that has sidelined him since January, but only one of Newcastle’s four summer signings (Sean Steur) starts.

Welcome to live coverage of Newcastle United’s pre-season friendly against North-East neighbours Gateshead. Eddie Howe’s side make the three-mile journey south of the River Tyne having beaten Darlington 3-0 in their first outing of the summer last weekend. The Magpies’ National League opponents this afternoon, helmed by former Sunderland captain Lee Cattermole, have already played three times in pre-season, thrashing Blyth 6-0 and drawing against Heaton Stannington and Hebburn Town. The Heed threatened a shock win in their last meeting with Newcastle three summers’ ago, leading 2-0 at the interval before conceding three second-half goals.

This contest at Gateshead International Stadium will be Newcastle’s first match since the death of Kevin Keegan and the club have confirmed that a minute of silence will be observed before kick-off. Newcastle’s men’s, women’s and academy teams will wear black armbands for all pre-season matches this summer.

Newcastle United's men's, women's and Under-21s teams will wear black armbands across all pre-season matches this summer as the club honours the life of Kevin Keegan.Full details ⤵️

Newcastle will welcome Liverpool, with whom Keegan enjoyed success in the 1970s, to St James’ Park for their Premier League opener, and the two sides are in talks over a suitable pre-match tribute. Flowers, messages and mementos have been laid outside Newcastle’s ground since Keegan’s death on Monday, including a heartfelt message penned by fellow club legend Alan Shearer, which read: “I hope you realised how much you meant, to me, to this club, to everyone. Thank you does not seem enough. Rest In Peace Boss. Alan Shearer.”

With regards to the football, there is an acceptance among Newcastle supporters that, having finished 12th in the Premier League last season and lost Anthony Gordon, Kieran Trippier and Sandro Tonali, this is a summer of transition. The uncertainty surrounding the future of £100m-rated club captain Bruno Guimarães, who is on the radar of Arsenal, will be a concern; Newcastle will be keen to avoid a repeat of the furore that circled Alexander Isak’s departure last summer. Guimarães will join the team next week following his World Cup exploits with Brazil and is expected to take part in Newcastle’s La Manga training camp, which starts on July 31.

Summer signings Sean Steur and Ewen Jaouen were each handed 45 minutes in the behind-closed-doors victory over Darlington, during which Howe used different XIs for the two halves. Bazoumana Touré – the £50m winger acquired from Hoffenheim – is expected to feature today having returned from his post-World Cup holiday. Yesterday Newcastle announced the arrival of midfielder Aladji Bamba, the France youth international, from Monaco and he was immediately integrated into team training. There is every possibility that he will feature this afternoon. Gateshead this week announced two signings of their own, as Luke Supyk, the New Zealand Under-20 forward, agreed a two-year deal having scored three goals in pre-season as a trialist. Defender Jack Robinson also joined the club.
