#1918. Hearts calamity in Switzerland: gift-wrapped goals, another injury and a 19y/o debut

Depleted Hearts’ Conference League bruising was almost totally self-inflicted in a 3-1 defeat by Thun in Switzerland.

Belgian boss Wouter Vrancken was without 10 players through various ailments and the Scottish outfit were dealt another blow in the 22nd minute when defender Jamie McCart put through his own goal in calamitous fashion.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Thun doubled their lead in the 33rd minute through striker Brighton Labeau after more poor defending, this time from skipper Stephen Kingsley – who went off later with an injury – and then Furkan Dursun grabbed a third in the 56th minute before Jambos defender Stuart Findlay reduced the deficit in the 82nd minute with a header.

Hearts are left with one Conference League point out of nine following a 1-1 home draw against Nordsjaelland and a 2-0 defeat away to Trabzonspor.

Thick smoke from a pyro halted the game soon after kick-off but when play resumed after a lengthy delay – there were nine minutes added on at the end of the first half – Hearts winger Josh McPake drew a save from Niklas Steffen with an angled drive that lacked real power.

In the 20th minute McPake’s effort from 25 yards after he had drifted in from the left had the power but was beaten away by the Thun keeper.

There appeared to be nothing untoward on the horizon but then came a Hearts horror show.

There was no real pressure on the Jambos goal when a long ball came into the box but with Lucien Dahler at his shoulder, a simple pass back from McCart somehow evaded Hearts keeper Beau Reus and slipped into the corner of the net.

Thun’s second goal was also gift-wrapped.

The home side broke clear and with pace following a Heart set-piece and when Nils Reichmuth crossed into the box from the right, Kingsley stuck out a leg to clear but the ball went straight to Labeau who swept it into the net from 10 yards out.

Dursun was shown a yellow card for a forearm challenge into the face of Findlay, and it perhaps deserved more punishment.

The interval gave the Tynecastle side time to reset but three minutes after the break, Reus made a diving save from Dursun and an even better one from Reichmuth moments later. However, the keeper was beaten once again when Dursun got his toe to a Reichmuth cross.

On the hour mark, Nico Maier raced clear of the Hearts defence but although his chip beat Reus, it sped wide of the target.

The night got worse for the rattled visitors as injured Kingsley was replaced by 19-year-old debutant Matthew Gillies, called back from a loan spell at Stenhousemuir. Hearts were sporadic in their threat.

Malachi Fagan-Walcott’s header from a Jordi Altena free-kick was brilliantly saved by Steffen.

In the 78th minute Jan Bamert had the ball in the net after Steffen tipped a free-kick from substitute Nassim Zoukit on to the bar but was ruled offside, before Findlay headed in a consolation from another Altena free-kick.

#1917. Hinshelwood: We can be vulnerable – but we’ll learn from Sutton defeat

Three goals in a 12-minute first-half spell put Chris Agutter’s team 3-0 up at Woodside Road on Saturday – and the Rebels were unable to find one their trademark second-half recoveries.

A disappointing afternoon ended with a number of Reds players with bruises and knocks and unable to play in Tuesday night’s National League Cup tie at home to Fulham under-21s.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

But it was a first defeat in 11 league games, and the Rebels’ job now is to show it was a blip in a fine first half of the season.

On Tuesday night Joel Colbran’s first goal of the season and an own goal by Nazim Benchaita five minutes from time earned Worthing a 2-1 home win over Fulham U21s in the National League Cup.

The Reds now have a blank weekend ahead and resume their league programme at Scunthorpe on Saturday week, where Hinshelwood will be looking for a more resilient defensive showing than he saw versus Sutton.

Hinshelwood said: “We didn’t turn up in the first half. We were too soft in conceding three goals in little over 10 minutes and just didn’t deal with things – like the long throw that led to their first goal and the long ball that resulted in their second.

"We’ve watched it all back and analysed it – it’s things we cannot do at this level. We have to learn from it and move on quickly.”

Hinshelwood said the disappointing thing was that Sutton’s disruptive approach – their shape and game-plan – was no surprise. He felt Worthing should have been much more ready to deal with it.

"We’re a young side and we do show vulnerability at times. We mustn’t dwell on it,” he said.

"Some of Sutton’s challenges were borderline. We were left with two or three who were battered and bruised and unable to play Tuesday. Someone said it was like watching football in the 1970s."

Just four days earlier Worthing had recovered from being 2-0 and 3-2 at home to Southend to draw 3-3.

But Hinshelwood said: “On Saturday you were waiting for that moment when we could get it back to 3-1 but it never came. We have to realise that we won’t always be able to fight back into a game as we have done a few times.”

Injury-wise, Dom Hutchinson and Harry Ransom are out for another eight and six weeks respectively with wrist fractures, while Sam Packham needs hamstring op.

#1916. Liverpool transfer news: Reds in ‘advanced talks’ over new contract for player ‘trusted’ by Andoni Iraola

By Oliver Thomas | 05 Nov 2026 12:02

Liverpool have reportedly entered advanced negotiations with teenage starlet Trey Nyoni over a new contract.

The Reds suffered a disappointing 3-2 Champions League defeat away against Fenerbahce on Wednesday, but it was a memorable night for Nyoni who scored his first goal for the club.

At the age of 19 years and 127 days, Nyoni became the youngest player in the club's history to score his first goal for the team in a European Cup match, while he is Liverpool’s second youngest Champions League goalscorer after Trent Alexander-Arnold.

Nyoni has stepped up to Andoni Iraola’s first team this season after the Reds rejected a £30m offer from Nottingham Forest during the summer transfer window.

The academy graduate was handed his first Premier League start for Liverpool in their 1-0 defeat to champions Arsenal at Anfield last weekend and has played 12 times for the Reds across all competitions this term.

Nyoni has made a notable impression in Iraola’s midfield playing alongside either Alexis Mac Allister, Dominik Szoboszlai or Ryan Gravenberch, and the youngster could soon be rewarded with an improved deal.

According to The Athletic, Nyoni is in advanced talks with Liverpool over extending his contract, even though his current deal runs until June 2030.

The report adds that Nyoni has been discussing his future with Liverpool for 'months', with the club keen to reward him with fresh terms to reflect his first-team emergence under Iraola.

While a contract extension has yet to be finalised, it is understood that there is optimism that an agreement will be reached, with a breakthrough in negotiations expected soon.

Speaking to reporters before Liverpool’s loss to Fenerbahce, Iraola made it clear that he believes Nyoni is now “in a very good place” to enhance his development.

“Trey just has to continue in the same way as since the beginning of pre-season, be ready for all of the games,” said the Spaniard.

“We trust him, he’s doing very well. We have to encourage him to continue learning, improving and getting experience. But he’s in a very good place.”

With Gravenberch facing a spell on the sidelines through injury and Szoboszlai having only just recovered from an injury of his own, Nyoni is a strong contender to start again for Liverpool in Sunday’s Premier League clash against Crystal Palace.

The 26-year-old immediately signalled to the Swansea coaching staff that he was unable to continue and was replaced by Benjamin Cabango with just 24 minutes on the clock.

"Welshy's scan is clear. It's just really a bad knock so there's nothing major," said Swansea head coach Vitor Matos.

#1914. CM: Dalot could reunite with Amorim at Milan as Man Utd deal winds down

Diogo Dalot has once again been linked with a potential return to AC Milan, where he spent the 2020-21 season on loan.

Calciomercato.com report that Roma’s visit to face Manchester United at Old Trafford will not only be an opportunity for the Giallorossi to face and perhaps erase the ghosts of the past, but also to watch someone up close who could be a name for the not-too-distant future: Diogo Dalot.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The Portuguese full-back’s contract is expiring at the end of next season and although he is happy in Manchester, many clubs are beginning to ask his entourage for details.

Roma were one step away from landing the defender in the summer of 2021 when the Portuguese coach José Mourinho was on the bench. The negotiations dragged on for a long time, but in the end it didn’t go through.

The reason ended up being quite simple: the Red Devils never agreed to a loan with option to buy formula while Roma – who were still severely limited by Financial Fair Play limitations – could not offer anything more.

Dalot knows Italy and Serie A well, and he recently spoke about his loan experience with Milan in an interview with The Player’s Tribune.

“It was one of the most important years of my career. I remember the way the club welcomed me and how welcome I felt in a year that was important to me, one in which I needed to regain my confidence in my football. Milan helped me get back to those levels,” he said.

“Every day, Paolo Maldini was on the sidelines to watch us train. Rain, shine, or cold, he was always there, in a suit and tie. He would say to me: ‘Mark like this’ or ‘Tackle it.’ Other times, he would scold me for trying too hard. ‘You’re an extraordinary player, don’t worry, you’ll see, everything will be fine’.”

As mentioned, Dalot’s deal expires in 2028 but there is the presence of a one-year clause that United can trigger. There are a number of teams monitoring his situation including Inter, Milan and Juventus, who have all enquired in recent weeks.

Nothing concrete has emerged yet, as Dalot happy in Manchester and isn’t thinking about the future. However, if things don’t change, a departure – perhaps even for a low-cost fee – could become a realistic possibility.

With the Rossoneri needing defenders, could they try pounce on a reunion for a versatile player that they and Ruben Amorim know well?

#1913. Rare win at Culver Road banishes Robins' Lancing demons and books Peter Bentley Cup quarter final spot

James Westlake described Hassocks as terrible on their Southern Combination Premier Division visit to Lancing 17 days ago when the Robins collapsed from 1-0 up on 87 minutes to lose 3-1.

Their mission returning to the GoCardless Stadium in the Peter Bentley League Cup a little over two weeks later was therefore clear. Come away with victory in whatever manner possible from a place where no Hassocks side had won in their past 11 visits stretching all the way back to September 2004 and a 6-2 success in this same competition.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Goals from corners scored by centre back pairing Dan Turner and Liam Hendy got the job done in a gritty 2-1 victory. Hardly a classic but the Robins will not care given what happened last time and their woeful record at Culver Road over the past 22 years. Their reward is a home quarter final against Lingfield.

Hassocks had the better first half chances only to be frustrated by the woodwork and Lancers goalkeeper Elliot Dailly. Lewis Finney shot too high with the first real opportunity on 25 minutes before Dailly made a smart save with his legs to deny Lewis Croal from close range.

Jack Troak has not taken many free kicks for the Robins in the past but he has surely jumped up the pecking order after rattling the bar with a brilliant curling effort from 25 yards.

The rebound fell kindly for tall striker Jamie Wilkes, whose header towards the bottom corner was clawed out by the sprawling Dailly.

Five minutes before the break saw Dailly make his best save of the night. Raging Joe Bull crossed for Darren Budd to produce a superb first touch and layoff to Troak.

Dailly could only have seen Troak's powerful drive late as it came at him between Scott Packer and Dylan Hurst. Somehow, Dailly managed to react and touch the shot from Troak onto the post.

The first 25 minutes of the second half were a non-event. Lancing tightened up defensively to stifle Hassocks going forward, meaning there was no repeat of the opportunities the Robins had managed to muster during the opening 45. And with the Lancers showing little inclination to attack themselves, it all became rather tedious.

Attention amongst the away contingent gathered behind the goal strayed so far as to wonder why Hassocks chairman Pat Harding was wearing a pair of leather gloves which looked like they should belong to a Spitfire pilot.

Rather aptly, it was a Robin currently sporting a delightful World War II moustache who fired Hassocks ahead on 72 minutes as Hendy breathed new and much-needed life into the tie.

Finney released substitute Joe Turner with a lovely through ball down the right channel. Turner made his way to the by-line to deliver a cross blocked behind by Packer.

The resulting corner was taken by Finney. Packer could only half clear to Hendy, who drilled a clinical shot into the bottom corner.

Celebrations were somewhat muted, probably because Hendy made over 250 appearances for Lancing during 10 years at Culver Road earlier in his career.

Hendy and Lancing have history in the Peter Bentley Cup too; he netted the opening goal in the 2016 final when the Lancers beat Newhaven 2-1 to lift the trophy for the first and so far only time.

Falling behind meant Lancing had to become more positive in an attempt to get back into the game. Gabriel Robinson should have done better after Dan Turner failed to deal with an Archie McGonigle clip over the top. Robinson could only put a weak one-on-one effort a long way wide.

Ed Cooper then almost got caught out by a long Alek Amissah pass forward. Hendy ducked out of a header, allowing the pass to travel all the way back to Cooper.

All looked fine until Cooper charged outside his box and only realised he had gone too far as the ball zipped past him. In the end, Cooper did well to chase back towards his goal and throw himself on top of the ball just before Antoine Sharpe beat him to it.

With the Lancers stirring, this had shades of the league game when Hassocks were monumentally punished for not getting a second goal. Over to Dan Turner to provide one on this occasion with 13 minutes remaining.

Finney looped another fine corner delivery towards the far post. Troak won a towering header back across goal which Turner met with a technically excellent volley. Dailly got a hand to it but there was far too much power in the shot for him to keep it out.

The two-goal cushion lasted only four minutes as Lancing pulled one back with a really well-worked move to set up a nervous finale.

McGonigle kicked things off deep inside the Lancers half. Mo Khedidji and Robinson combined to return the ball to McGonigle, now breaking down the left beyond the Hassocks backline.

His square pass across the edge of the box tempted Cooper from his line. Sharpe got their first, going around Cooper and firing into the unguarded net.

Now thoughts amongst the travelling support really did flash back 17 days. Hassocks though showed themselves in no mood for a repeat and it was in fact the Robins who looked the more likely scorers in the final 10.

Troak bent another free kick on target and also fired a shot a long way over after being teed up by Omar Abdsami. The only moment of alarm at the other end came when Dylan Walter crossed from the right but Cooper averted any danger by making a diving punch clear.

Hassocks: Cooper; Bonwick-Adams, D Turner, Hendy, Bull; Wilkes, Budd; Fender, Finney, Troak; Croal.

Subs: Benson, Turner, Abdsami, Blake (used), Bromage (unused).

#1912. Fortuna Sittard vs Telstar - prediction, team news, lineups

By Adepoju Marvellous | 05 Nov 2026 12:26

High-flying Fortuna Sittard return to Eredivisie action this weekend, hosting Telstar at the Fortuna Sittard Stadion on Saturday.

The home side begin this weekend’s round of fixtures in sixth place with 19 points - 10 places and 10 points clear of the visitors.

A trip to Feyenoord, who had won three straight meetings between the teams, threatened to end Fortuna’s six-game unbeaten run, especially after Luciano Valente opened the scoring just before the hour mark. However, Shiloh ‘t Zand equalised with four minutes remaining to force a share of the spoils.

While some may argue the point flattered Danny Buijs’s men given their performance, it was a reward for their resilience, a quality they have displayed in abundance since a 5-1 drubbing at the hands of Ajax in mid-September.

Having collected just seven points from a possible 15 in Sittard-Geleen, Fortuna’s return to form still has room for improvement via consistent results at home. A 1-0 win over Excelsior in their last home outing suggests they are moving in the right direction.

Bottom of the league in average ball possession this term (35.7%), Fortuna remain a side best known for their off-the-ball work. They finished second-bottom in this metric last season, only ahead of relegated Heracles.

With each of their next six matches coming against teams currently below them in the table, Fortuna have an opportunity to build a sustained run of positive results and enter the second half of the season well positioned for a European push.

After almost three months, Telstar finally ended their wait for a first victory since beating NEC Nijmegen on the opening weekend, running out emphatic 4-2 winners over FC Utrecht in Sunday’s clash at BUKO Stadion.

The victory came at a crucial time for manager Henk Brugge, who was under increased scrutiny after his side were knocked out of the KNVB Beker first round by lower-league opposition Almere City just four days earlier.

Two points adrift of safety, another Telstar defeat this weekend could pile the pressure back on Brugge and their away record this season has been dismal, with just one win, four points, and four goals scored from five matches on the road.

However, De Witte Leeuwen are unbeaten in their last five trips to the Fortuna Sittard Stadion dating back to August 2014, and will draw confidence from their most recent trip in March, when they cruised to a 4-1 victory.

Facing a side with the best big-chance conversion rate in the division (76.9%), Saturday’s visitors will be wary of conceding too many opportunities, despite boasting a significant advantage in clear-cut chances created (23-10).

Rodrigo Guth and Lequincio Zeefuik both limped off with injuries in Fortuna’s last outing and are doubtful for Saturday’s clash.

This could open the door for Ivan Marquez and Kristoffer Peterson - both substitutes last time out - to come into the hosts’ starting lineup.

Twenty-one-year-old Gerald Alders has missed Telstar’s last three outings and remains a doubt for this weekend.

Patrick Brouwer and Rui Mendes were also absent against Utrecht, although the former is likely to return to action in Sittard.

Tyrone Owusu has scored five goals and provided one assist in his last five matches for the visitors, making the midfielder one to watch.

Fortuna Sittard possible starting lineup:

Branderhorst; Pinto, Van Ottele, Marquez, Hubner, Dahlhaus; Ihattaren, Descotte, Brittijn, ‘t Zand; Zeefuik

Koeman Jr; Peersman, Soualhia, Valk, Caschili; Rossen, Ahmed; Demircan, Owusu, Martha; Thorisson

Fortuna are playing their best football in some time, and that momentum makes them strong favourites to edge an out-of-sorts Telstar side.

We expect the home side to make light work of their visitors and head into the international break on a high.

#1911. Wouter Vrancken's Hearts message after Swiss setback - 'we have to stick together'

Wouter Vrancken insists Hearts will have to stick together following their self-inflicted 3-1 Conference League defeat by Thun in Switzerland.

The Scottish outfit, without 10 players through various injuries, fell behind in the 22nd minute when defender Jamie McCart knocked the ball into his own net.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Thun doubled their lead in the 33rd minute through striker Brighton Labeau after a poor attempted clearance from captain Stephen Kingsley – who went off later with an injury – and then Furkan Dursun grabbed a third in the 56th minute.

Jambos defender Stuart Findlay then gave some unrealised hope of a comeback in the 82nd minute when he headed in from close range.

After three Conference League fixtures Hearts have one point out of nine and have won just two of their last 10 fixtures in all competitions.

Vrancken told TNT Sports: “Like I said already to the guys, we have to stick together now. We know which situation we’re in with all the circumstances.

“And there’s only one thing that you have to do now and that is stick together and keep working hard. In general, it was not good enough in quality and can you blame them?

“Yeah, on one hand you can because you want to always expect the best and want the best. On the other hand, I’m still proud of what they did already in the run-up games.”

Kingsley was replaced in the second half by 19-year-old Matthew Gillies, called back from a loan spell at Stenhousemuir amid the club’s injury crisis, and Vrancken admitted there was an element of risk playing him on the artificial surface which the Jambos boss had criticised.

He said: “We talked it through before the game of course, a few days before the game. And yeah, it’s always a risk, especially when it’s another surface, and especially when it’s bad like that, but he was confident in playing and that’s where we are.”

Hearts’ next Conference League game is against Ligue 1 side in Monaco at Tynecastle on November 26 but Vrancken is more concerned about the home William Hill Premiership game against Falkirk on Sunday.

He said: “Monaco’s a really strong side, maybe the strongest side we will face in Europe. So we will see when we get there, because I think there are a lot of important games before that, especially on Sunday.”

The well-drilled Sarnies, now with seven wins on the spin, missed a penalty before grabbing the winner and moving to third in the table — three points behind Hollands men with a game in hand.

#1909. Celtic player ratings v Besiktas: game-changers produce late fireworks as trio of starters struggle

Marks out of ten for Celtic players after crucial 3-2 victory on matchday four of the Europa League

There were fireworks aplenty at Celtic Park on Bonfire Night as Martin O’Neill’s side produced a stunning late turnaround to claim a dramatic 3-2 victory over Besiktas and finally get their Europa League campaign up and running.

For long spells, this looked destined to be another miserable European evening for the Scottish champions. A dismal first-half performance was followed by Jordan Lotomba’s penalty concession and Junior Olaitan’s opener, leaving the Hoops staring down the barrel of a fourth consecutive league phase defeat.

However, the second-half introduction of Callum Osmand and Camilo Duran changed the complexion of the contest, with the substitutes turning a seemingly lost cause into a memorable comeback victory.

Osmand equalised before Duran struck twice, including an 87th-minute winner, after Orkun Kokcu had threatened to spoil the party with a stunning long-range effort.

It was a result Celtic desperately craved. Their European campaign had been in danger of unravelling after three successive defeats, following on from their failure to negotiate Champions League qualification against LASK. O’Neill had previously insisted there should be no ceiling on his side's continental ambitions, but with the games beginning to run out, this was effectively a must-win encounter.

Besiktas arrived in Glasgow in considerably better shape, sitting eighth in the 36-team standings after victories over Marseille and Hoffenheim and a draw with Crystal Palace. Celtic, meanwhile, were looking to avoid four consecutive defeats in major European competition for the first time since December 2017.

There were familiar faces in the visiting ranks, too. Vaclav Cerny returned to Parkhead following his controversial water-bottle incident involving Celtic supporters during Rangers’ 3-2 victory in March last year. Former Hoops striker Oh Hyeon-gyu also featured, while ex-Rangers defender Ridvan Yilmaz was named among the substitutes.

Fireworks provided some pre-match spectacle, but the atmosphere inside Parkhead was subdued, with a sparse home support reflecting the growing discontent surrounding the club.

The opening exchanges offered little to lift the mood. Celtic struggled to build any real momentum, while the loudest reaction from the home support came whenever Cerny found himself in possession.

The visitors gradually assumed control as Celtic struggled to keep hold of the ball. By the 39th minute, O’Neill's men had registered just two touches inside the opposition penalty area. Nygren's air shot inside the Besiktas box shortly before the interval provided an unfortunate summary of Celtic's attacking frustrations.

Celtic's evening took a turn for the worse in the 52nd minute. Jordan Lotomba, on his first start at right-back, made a rash sliding challenge on Poku right on the edge of the penalty area, with the contact occurring on the line. The referee had little hesitation in pointing to the spot.

Johnstone initially produced an excellent save to deny Olaitan, but the goalkeeper was left helpless as the Besiktas forward reacted quickest to convert the rebound.

At that stage, Celtic looked short of ideas and confidence, with the prospect of a fourth straight European defeat looming large.

Then came the turning point. O’Neill introduced Osmand, and the youngster needed just 43 seconds to make his mark. McGregor threaded a delightful reverse pass into his path, allowing the 20-year-old to take one touch before drilling a composed finish into the bottom corner.

The goal sparked an immediate transformation. Celtic suddenly had purpose and aggression, with the crowd responding to the renewed energy on the pitch. Scales went close to levelling matters when his deflected header was superbly clawed over the crossbar by Nubel, while Nygren subsequently dragged another opportunity narrowly wide after being picked out by Osmand.

Celtic's second goal felt increasingly inevitable. It arrived in the 78th minute, with Duran providing the finishing touch to another excellent attacking move. Having been shifted into the central striking position, the Colombian immediately demonstrated what he could offer through the middle, timing his run perfectly to latch onto Osmand's pass, round Nubel and slot into the unguarded net.

The hosts looked capable of adding to their tally in the closing stages, but Besiktas had one final response. Captain Orkun Kokcu, introduced from the bench, unleashed a sensational effort from around 25 yards that flew into the bottom-left corner, leaving Johnstone with no chance.

It was a devastating blow so late in the contest, but Celtic were not finished. Just two minutes later, Duran once again found space behind the visitors defence as Tierney's effort fell invitingly into his path. The Colombian showed excellent footwork to bring the ball under control before stabbing it beyond Nubel and restoring Celtic's lead.

This time, there would be no way back for the visitors. There is still plenty of ground to make up in the Europa League standings, but Celtic have at least given themselves something to build on with this result.

We give each player a mark out of ten for their display.

Kept his place despite conceding five goals in his previous three domestic games. Produced an excellent first-half save to tip Trossard’s ferocious, albeit offside, strike on to the crossbar. Strong right hand to keep out Olaitan’s penalty but couldn’t prevent the rebound. No chance of getting to Kokcu's 25-yard wonder strike. 6 | SNS Group

Making his first start since arriving from Feyenoord in the summer, he struggled to cope with the Turks’ threat down his side, often being dragged out of position and given the run-around. A rash challenge on Poku resulted in the penalty concession. Looked to make amends with a lung-busting run from his own half to the edge of the box, but unable to get a shot away. Withdrawn shortly after. 5 | PA

The ever-dependable American was rock solid throughout. Made an important early intervention to deny Trossard and produced arguably one of his best performances so far this season. Subbed late on. 7 | SNS Group

A sliding challenge prevented Cerny from testing the keeper early on. Lapse in concentration almost proved costly as Besiktas threatened midway through the first half. Fortunate to escape a boking for a shirt pull on Oh. Saw a deflected second-half header require a sharp save to claw it over the bar. 6 | SNS Group

#1908. Chelsea in 10-goal thriller as ‘Alonso ball’ brings risk and reward

Chelsea’s first match under the management of Xabi Alonso was a 10-goal thriller in Australia, as the Premier League side eventually showed their class in a 6-4 win over Western Sydney Wanderers.

Star striker João Pedro, who was controversially left out of Brazil’s World Cup squad, scored a nine-minute hat-trick after coming off the bench with half an hour of the friendly remaining.

Alonso had selected a youthful team for the first hour before bringing nine senior players, including João Pedro, into the side in the second half. According to Transfermarkt, Chelsea’s squad is valued at over £1.3bn while their opponents a more modest £5.86m.

Teenage signing Dastan Satpayev, midfielder Dario Essugo and winger Jamie Gittens also found the net for Chelsea, who were defensively vulnerable for long spells for the game.

Here are five things Telegraph Sport learned from Alonso’s first match.

João Pedro scored 13 goals in the second half of last season and his impressive performances resulted in the 24-year-old being named Chelsea’s player of the campaign. It was something of a surprise, then, when he was left out of Carlo Ancelotti’s Brazil squad this summer.

The good news for Chelsea is that João Pedro’s absence from the World Cup has given him plenty of time to recover ahead of the new campaign, and he looked thrillingly sharp in his second-half performance against Western Sydney Wanderers. The difference in class between João Pedro and Liam Delap, the man he replaced, was clear for all to see.

Two of the Brazilian’s three goals were classy, composed finishes — and he also created a goal for Gittens after surging past three defenders on the left wing. João Pedro looks like he means business.

As expected, Alonso tasked his players with deploying a possession-based strategy in which the ball is worked from back to front between the lines. At times, Alonso’s vision was executed in style: Chelsea’s two goals in the first half were both the consequence of slick passing moves.

There were plenty of other occasions, though, when Chelsea were sloppy in their passing and defensively exposed when they lost the ball. The best example of this was in the second half, when Estêvão’s error allowed Western Sydney Wanderers to score their fourth goal of the game.

Admittedly, Chelsea’s attempts to play passing football were not helped by the poor quality of the pitch in Sydney. A recent rugby game had created a bobbly, unpredictable surface which caused no end of problems for Chelsea’s midfield players. That may sound like an excuse for their sloppiness, but it is probably a fair one.

Chelsea started the game with two Reggies in their midfield. Reggie Walsh is a 17-year-old technician who last year became the club’s third-youngest player, and was loved by former head coach Enzo Maresca. He played as the No 10.

Reggie Watson, meanwhile, is the son of former Premier League midfielder Ben and is one of the most exciting talents in English football. A composed central midfielder, Watson is a regular for England’s youth teams and is the youngest player on Chelsea’s pre-season tour.

Both players showed glimpses of their talent in this match in Sydney. Watson was trusted with set-piece duties and produced some excellent deliveries, while also playing some lovely passes through the lines. Watson was the only Chelsea player to feature for the full 90 minutes, which spoke volumes of the quality of his performance.

Walsh was less involved but caught the eye in a couple of moments, not least when playing a delicate one-two with Essugo in advance of the midfielder’s first-half strike.

Satpayev is technically not a Chelsea player yet, as his deal officially commences when he turns 18 in August. His former club, Kairat, gave special dispensation to allow the teenager to join Chelsea’s pre-season tour ahead of the completion of his £3m transfer, which means he is officially in Australia as a “triallist”.

Satpayev is a player of obvious talent and has already played nine games for Kazakhstan. Before this move to Chelsea, he scored 21 goals in 41 games in the Kazakhstan Premier League.

The first sighting of Satpayev was an exciting one for Chelsea supporters, who saw the new man’s running speed and shooting power as he scored the opening goal of the game. Running in behind the Western Sydney Wanderers defence, Satpayev surged clear of the opposition and launched a scorching shot into the roof of the net.

Gittens endured a hugely disappointing first campaign at Chelsea last season, following his £52m move from Borussia Dortmund. Injury issues did not help his cause but he struggled to make much of an impact when he was fully fit, scoring just one goal in 27 appearances in all competitions.

Gittens is therefore a man with it all to prove at Stamford Bridge this season, and he has started the new campaign in promising form. His goal here came after two strikes in two behind-closed-doors friendly games before Chelsea left for Australia. Gittens was a constant threat after coming onto the pitch in the 63rd minute, showing his pace on the wing and his ability to go down the touchline or cut inside. His challenge now is to replicate this level of performance against better opposition.

A late revival ensures Chelsea win their first pre-season friendly under Xabi Alonso. There was a step up in class once Palmer, Pedro, Gittens, Estevao and Palestra were introduced, and the Australian side could not contain them. No injuries on a dogy pitching probably the biggest victory for the new manager.

Just the three minutes of added time to play.

Three goals in nine minutes for the Brazilian. Excellent corner delivery from Estevao, Fofana’s header blocked but then Joao Pedro turns home from close range. Baffling decision by Brazil not to take him to the World Cup.

Chelsea flooding forward again, and they have a corner in the last minute of normal time.

Chelsea now lead 5-4, Cole Palmer picking out Joao Pedro with the through ball but Western Sydney Wanderers were far too open. Joao Pedro shows his composure, sitting the defender down and rolling the ball into the bottom corner.

Estevao shows he has not lost his burst of speed after that serious hamstring injury but his shot flies straight into the side netting. Joao Pedro then delights the crowd with another piece of skill.

Jamie Gittens is having a good pre-season, having scored in two behind-closed-doors friendlies before this game in Australia. He has looked sharp since coming off the bench and has been involved in two of Chelsea’s goals.

Gittens had a disappointing first season at Chelsea following his £52m move from Dortmund last summer and is clearly keen to impress Alonso.

Robert Sanchez picks out Gittens with a raking pass, but his shot is blocked. The same is true for Joao Pedro’s follow up attempt. Gittens has impressed since coming on.

Poor defensive header back into a dangerous area from Gittens’s cross, but it is a crisp touch and finish from Joao Pedro, picking out the bottom corner. Chelsea level at 4-4. The move started with a quick free-kick, from Palmer, which he won.

Western Sydney Wanderers score their fourth goal of the game. Chelsea make another error when playing out from the back, it was Estevao who sold Reggie Watson short. One pass and one shot later, Awan Lual finishes beyond Sanchez.

Mazy run inside from Estevao off the right flank, but there was not quite enough power in his shot to beat the goalkeeper.

Joao Pedro is very good at taking the ball in and making it stick. Palestra looks very progressive from right-back, looks full of running and attacking intent.

Some of Western Sydney Wanderers’s corner routines have been quite nifty, Chelsea opened up from a short one again. Palmer with a velvety touch in midield and pass forward towards Palestra who was breaking forward.

Gittens scores, and the introduction of the senior players has made a difference already. Levi Colwill started the move with a longer pass forward, before Joao Pedro skips through challenges to tee up Gittens.

Nine changes made by Alonso: Palmer, Estevao, Palestra, Gittens, Sanchez, Colwill, Anselmino, Joao Pedro and Fofana are the players who have come on.

The Australian side now lead. Emenalo’s clearance deflects off a Western Sydney Wanderers player, and falls kindly to Scicluna, who drills his show beyond Sharman-Lowe into the bottom corner. He come the Chelsea changes.

Western Sydney Wanderers playing some good football in the last few minutes, Saptaev outmuscled in midfield and a shot comes in from the edge of the area. Sharman-Lowe saves, then Tosin clears after a short corner routine.

This young Chelsea side, which is still dealing with jet lag, looks a little tired now. They have not been under huge pressure but they can hardly complain about falling 3-2 behind. Here come all the big names, as Alonso makes huge changes for the last 30 minutes.

Chelsea enjoying a spell of comfortable possession, the tempo of the game has dropped. Good play again, from Reggie Watson, finding Emenalo on the overlap but he slices his shot high and wide when there was time to take aim.

Chelsea remain committed to passing out from the back, but the uneven pitch is making that difficult. Sharman-Lowe passes the ball straight out for a throw-in. Good defending from Acheampong to deal with a teasing cross.

Chelsea win a free-kick in a shooting position, and Reggie Watson takes it with his right foot. He goes goalkeeper’s side but, it shot curls just wide of the post.

Western Sydney Wanderers kick off in the second half.

Kellyman on for Essugo in midfield, and Nicoll-Jazuli replaces Kavuma-McQueen.

Some eye-catching football from Chelsea going forward, but some loose defending too. Suspect it is not long before we see Palmer, Estevao, Colwill and Joao Pedro. Walsh and Watson have done well in midfield for Chelsea.

Half-time! 🕰️Watch the second half LIVE on CFC+ 📺

Another really bad miss from Tosin. Free header from a corner, could see it all the way, but he skewed the ball wide from a just a couple of yards out. Chelsea should be in front.

Subuloye wins a back post header from the Chelsea corner, but the “home” team clear. More goals in this game, surely. Saptaev wins Chelsea a corner with another burst forward.

This is a great team goal. Essugo started the move, finding Saptaev down the left. Essugo moves the ball on two Walsh, who gives it him back with a slick one-two and Essugo rolls the ball into the bottom corner.

That’s the second impressive team goal that Chelsea have scored in this first half. Essugo to Walsh, Walsh to Essugo, Essugo finds the corner. Walsh, 17, has produced some nice touches in the No 10 position. Last year he became the third-youngest player in Chelsea’s history and you can see he is a supremely talented teenager.

Chelsea in trouble defensively again, passing their way into trouble on the edge of their defensive third. I’m sure there will be a raft of half-time changes, but that was probably the plan all along.

Chelsea have been alarmingly open and easy to play through. The collective structure and individual defending were both poor in advance of that second Western Sydney Wanderers goal. I expect they’ll tighten up when the more experienced players come into the game.

Hammond is the goalscorer, and it is a finish of genuine quality. Silky touch to flick the ball inside Josh Acheampong, and fire low into the bottom corner. Soft Chelsea defending, though.

Smooth combination play from Walsh and Watson, the two Reggies in Chelsea’s midfield, before Saptaev shoots over the bar form the edge of the box. A shame for marketing people and headline writers that one of Walsh or Watson are not called Ronnie.

Reggie Watson with a foul in midfield. Fair to say Chelsea’s youthful team are on the back foot now, but there was nice turn in midfield from Essugo after more passing out from the back. Clear that is an emphasis for Alonso.

Sharman-Lowe claims a cross, but Western Sydney Wanderers down their right flank again. I almost anticipated a hydration break at this stage, but it is back to business as usual. Chelsea flagging a touch after a lively start.

Chelsea’s defence looking a touch exposed again, but Borrello curls a shot wide of the post. Emenalo has down well going forward but there was space down his side there.

Two causes for concern for Chelsea in the first 15 minutes here. The first is the pitch in Sydney, which looks terrible. The ball is bobbling all over midfield, making it very difficult for Chelsea’s central players in particular. The second concern will be their defending for that set-piece, as Western Sydney Wanderers had two free headers.

Liam Delap has not been particularly involved, but Reggie Watson almost found him with a cute reverse pass. Watson the plays a progressive pass forward from deep.

Reggie Walsh pushes forward and takes on a shot from long range. Well struck, another save from the goalkeeper. From the resulting corner, taken by Watson, Tosin misses a free header. Good chance, should have hit the target.

Chelsea concede from the corner. Flicked on at the near post and a free header at the back stick for Anthony Pantazopoulos. One for Austin MacPhee, Chelsea’ new set-piece coach, to clip up and show in the team meeting.

Emenalo fouled after more neat football out from the back by Chelsea. Alonso is on his feet on the touchline, barking instructions. Emenalo has showed some silky touches.

Chance for Western Sydney Wanderers though, nut Sharman-Lowe tips Gillion’s shot around the post.

The pitch is very, very bobbly. Excellent strike from Kavuma-McQueen for Chelsea, but Holmes tips the shot around the post.

Was that the first glimpse of “Alonso-ball”? It’s a lovely team goal, worked from back to front with some incisive passing. Terrific, powerful finish by Dastan Satpayev, the 17-year-old Kazakh, who joined from FC Kairat this summer. He already has nine caps for Kazakhstan.

Technically speaking, Satpayev is not officially a Chelsea player yet and is a “triallist” on this tour. He will be formally unveiled when he turns 18 in August.

The 17-year-old summer signing from Kairat Almaty has put Chelsea in front. It was a nice move from their own defensive third, drawing Western Sydney Wanderers on creating a two-on-two against their defence. Satpaev goes through and blasts a shot into the roof of the net. Good through ball from Ryan Kavuma-McQueen.

Chelsea youngsters Walsh and Watson do well in midfield, and they have a free-kick on halfway. Reggie Watson is the son of former Crystal Palace and Wigan Athletic midfielder Ben. A couple of stray kicks from Chelsea’s goalkeeper Teddy Sharman-Lowe. An opening for the hosts, but Hammond’s strike is wayward.

Landon Emenalo is playing at left wing-back, and he is the son of former Chelsea director of football Michael. He has had one burst forward already, and is called into some early defending to concede a throw in.

Chelsea get the game under way. The pitch looks very patchy. Incredible how clubs are willing to play mutli-million pound assets on surfaces like this.

Western Sydney Wanderers in horizontal red and black stripes, Chelsea in the season’s new blue home kit.

Off the bus. 🚎 pic.twitter.com/0sBDuEtzog

#1905. Celtic cure insomnia before subs make the difference to spark Europa League lift-off

Goals from the bench as Celtic come from behind to claim 3-2 win over Besiktas

Celtic are up and running in the Europa League at the fourth time of asking after a crucial 3-2 home win over Besiktas.

After losing their opening three games, Celtic needed a positive result against the Turkish side and showed fortitude to come back from a goal down to breathe life into their aspirations of reaching the knock-out stages.

They were thankful for supersubs Callum Osmand and Camilo Duran, who came on to rescue the match for Celtic in an action-packed second half following Besiktas' 54th-minute opener. The win leaves Celtic in 32nd place with three points at the halfway stage of the main phase.

Celtic travel to Torreense of Portugal and Cypriot outfit Omonia later this year before matches against Marseille (home) and Union (away) in January. They can head into those fixtures with some optimism after a much-needed victory, only their fourth in 11 matches across all competitions.

Manager Martin O'Neill came into this match under pressure following Sunday's 2-0 defeat by Falkirk. The 74-year-old rotated his team, giving rare starts to right-back Jordan Lotomba and winger James Forrest, and introduced his key players at the right time.

The first half could have been bottled up and used as an insomnia cure. Celtic had one shot and two legitimate touches in the Besiktas penalty box. The Turkish side did little of note either, their former Rangers winger Vaclav Cerny routinely jeered.

Mercifully, the second half was far better.

Besiktas took the lead on 54 in calamitous circumstances. Celtic goalkeeper Sam Johnstone walloped a clearance off Leandro Trossard and the ball squirted to Ernest Poku. He absolutely skinned Lotomba, who chopped down the winger with his flailing attempt to salvage the situation. It was a clear spot-kick and while Johnstone partially redeemed himself by saving Olaitan's powerful penalty, the ball spun into the sky and towards the goal, where Olaitan followed up to tap home.

Lotomba tried to recover with a surging run from his own penalty box on 59 minutes that got the home crowd briefly energised. It was his last act, replaced by Colby Donovan on the hour mark. Duran and Osmand were also brought on for Forrest and Sebastien Tounekti.

Osmand did more in the first minute of action than the powderpuff Tounekti did in 60. The Englishman immediately made an impact, with Callum McGregor seizing on a loose ball and feeding the forward to find the bottom corner of Alexander Nubel's goal with an accurate strike. Celtic had something to build upon.

Besiktas had played comfortably up until this point but now looked a little rattled. Celtic embarked on their best period of the match. Nubel reacted smartly on 67 minutes to save a netbound Liam Scales header. Benjamin Nygren whistled an effort just over the bar eight minutes later. Suddenly the game was there for Celtic.

The ineffective striker Kasper Hogh was subbed off for Haissem Hassan as O'Neill turned to the Egyptian to unlock the Besiktas defence. But it was two earlier subs who made the difference again on 77 minutes, with Osmand slipping Duran in for the Colombian to round Nubel and send Celtic Park wild.

Celtic now had to hold on but their resistance was pierced by a vicious strike from Besiktas sub Orkun Kokcu from 25 yards on 86 minutes that fizzed beyond Johnstone and into the net. Never mind, though, when Duran is in town. The Colombian took in a sclaffed cross from Kieran Tierney a minute later and netted.

And this time, it was job done. Celtic Park roared its approval at full time.

Camarda was present at the Paolo and Larissa Pini Institute for a one-on-one discussion with students and a lesson with the Sport and Health tutors, to help promote the value of sport and the desire to continue practicing it.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It was the player who asked the students questions for the most part, not the other way around. Camarda questioned them on their motivations behind playing sports, if they have ever considered quitting and if so why they chose to continue.

“That’s the beauty of sport: it gives you the chance to test yourself, have fun, and improve, even when you don’t succeed at something.

Camarda himself is having to be patient and to wait for opportunities at the moment given his lack of playing time under Ruben Amorim, which may even mean evaluating another loan move away from his boyhood club.

#1903. Why Celtic bench heroes did not start against Besiktas as Martin O'Neill explains decision-making

Celtic manager Martin O'Neill made no apologies for keeping his Europa League heroes in reserve - revealing it was always the plan to unleash goalscorers Camilo Duran and Callum Osman on Besiktas at the hour mark.

Duran netted twice and Osmand also popped up with a goal as Celtic defeated Besiktas 3-2 in Glasgow to breathe life into their Europa League campaign.

Celtic needed a victory after three opening losses in the competition and now sit 32nd in the standings. O'Neill believes the win over what he labelled "a fine Besiktas side" gives them a chance of progression to the knockout stages.

The 74-year-old rotated his team due to fatigue and a heavy schedule, and deserved praise for bringing on Duran and Osmand - his most dynamic forwards - when the game became open.

"I'm not standing up for myself, absolutely not, not at all," said O'Neill. "It was designed to do exactly what it did. We have been playing Sunday, Thursday, Sunday, Thursday, Wednesday, whatever day it happens to be. We have played, I don't know what, nine games in 23 days or 24 days.

O'Neill urged his Celtic team to build on the victory both in the Premiership and in Europe, with Kilmarnock visiting Parkhead on Sunday. He also hailed the character of his players for recovering from the concession of the opener and then a late leveller.

#1901. England squad: Choose Thomas Tuchel's 26 players for Spain, Croatia fixtures

By Ben Knapton | 05 Nov 2026 12:47

A spot in the UEFA Nations League knockout stages is on the line for England when they complete their League A campaign against Spain and Croatia during the November international break.

Thomas Tuchel's side kicked off Group 3 on a sour note with a 3-2 home defeat to the world champions, but back-to-back victories over the Czech Republic and a 7-0 crushing of Croatia on the road have put them on the brink of progression.

The Three Lions just need one point from their final two games to progress to the quarter-finals, and here, Sports Mole gives you the chance to pick your England squad for the November international break - be sure to download and share with your friends!

Tuchel should have no major quandaries on the goalkeeping front, as James Trafford and Jordan Pickford are shoo-ins, while Dean Henderson is likely to displace Brighton & Hove Albion veteran Jason Steele after recovering from injury.

However, the England boss now faces the age-old Ben White dilemma in defence, as the Arsenal right-back has stayed injury-free in recent weeks and has enjoyed a strong start to the campaign with the Premier League champions.

White has provided three assists in 12 games for the Gunners while starting seven of their nine top-flight fixtures, but he has not been selected for England since March; a hamstring injury ruled him out of the extended September/October period.

Tuchel must also weigh up whether to recall Harry Maguire, who has been a stalwart in an under-performing Manchester United side, and Djed Spence, who has forced his way into the Inter Milan XI after recovering from injury.

The biggest dilemma for the former Chelsea head coach undoubtedly comes in the final third of the field, though, as all eyes will be on whether Blues playmaker Cole Palmer is included in Tuchel's ranks.

Palmer pulled out of the September/October squad through injury, triggering a frustrated response from Tuchel, who admitted that the 24-year-old misses too many camps and his England future is potentially in jeopardy under the current regime.

However, a fully-fit Palmer could be offered a route back into the squad due to Bukayo Saka's injury, as the Arsenal winger is expected to be out until December with the quadriceps problem he sustained against Bayern Munich in the Champions League.

Noni Madueke and Phil Foden will also be fighting for attacking recalls, although the latter - who was also snubbed from the World Cup group - has already suggested that the November squad may come a little too soon for him.

Madueke, on the other hand, may be directly competing with Arsenal teammate Eberechi Eze, who was included in the September/October selection despite his fringe status at the Emirates.

Meanwhile, Dominic Calvert-Lewin was summoned to play second fiddle to Harry Kane last month, but having scored just once in his last five Premier League games, the Leeds United striker's spot could come under threat from Ollie Watkins.

#1900. Broadbridge Heath taste Sussex derby success – Horsham YM well-beaten by United

Broadbridge Heath 2-1 Crowborough Athletic

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Broadbridge Heath welcomed Crowborough Athletic to the Air Engineering Stadium for this midweek clash between two former Southern Combination League clubs but it was Bears manager Chris Simmons’ side that picked up the points.

Crowborough came into the game on a run of four games unbeaten and they started on the front foot forcing a corner in the opening minutes which saw the ball come out to the lively Rushaar Samuel-Smikle who hit a right foot shot high and wide of target.

On 18 minutes George Hutcheon won the ball off a Heath defender wide on the right and played it inside to Harry Forster, who played it into the path of Findlay Chapman. He struck a fierce right foot shot from the edge of the penalty area that was saved brilliantly by Alfie Hadfield diving across to his left to push the ball out for a corner.

The half continued that way with the Crows pressing high up the pitch and preventing Simmons’ side from playing their free-flowing football and it was no real surprise when the visitors took the lead on 24 minutes.

Marcus Goldsmith won the ball wide on the right and just inside the Broadbridge Heath half, the Crows skipper played a long diagonal right foot cross into the penalty area to Harry Forster who leaped like a salmon to place a looping header over Hadfield and into the net.

On 30 minutes another Crows interception, this time by Hutceon, saw him win the ball wide on the right on the halfway line and playing it forward to Samuel-Smikle who advanced towards goal before he cut inside on to his left foot and hit a shot just wide of the far post.

With 5 minutes of the half remaining Forster received the ball in the middle of the park and played it forward to Goldsmith who then picked a pass to Samuel-Smikle who hammered a right foot shot just wide of the post and it remained 0-1 at the break.

Whatever was said in the Broadbridge Heath changing room at half-time certainly had an impact on the game with the Bears more lively, sharper and passing far more accurate than before.

They equalised on 64 minutes when Ben Royall received the ball in the left back position and drove forward before playing the ball to the feet of Sam Hards who played a pass between two defenders to allow Zac Jeanes to get away down the left flank.

The Heath forward took the ball to the goal-line before playing a pass across the face of goal to Charlie Connell in acres of space for a simple tap-in.

The game was changed completely within a minute of the restart when Sal Marino played a diagonal pass from the halfway line down the left channel to Jeanes who played it inside towards Sam Church. A defender intercepted the pass but only managed to play it straight to Sam Hards some 14 yards from goal who dispatched a low left foot shot that flew under the diving Charlie Holmwood to give the Bears the lead.

It was the fifth straight game that young Hards had got on the scoresheet.

The Bears continued to create chances with Lewis Hyde heading a Jeanes free kick just wide of the post, Zac Young trying a long range shot that was gathered comfortably by Holmwood and a goalmouth scramble saw the ball ping around the 6 yard box. But the game ended with a win for the Bears in what can best be described as the proverbial ‘game of two halves’.

Simmons said afterwards: “It was a really disappointing 1st half performance, they out worked and out fought us and our quality on the ball was poor, 2nd half was better, our equaliser was more like us and then Sam continued his great form with the winner.”

BBH: Hadfield, Richardson, Royall, Holden, Hyde (Salaam 77), Peters, Young (Rawlins 90), Church (Marino 70), Hards, Connell, Mann (Jeanes 60).

Under constant pressure YM kept scrapping, and Eastbourne keeper Alieu Secka had to rush out to smother the ball – until, with little time left, sub Baran Kartel twisted the knife with the visitor’s fifth goal.

#1899. Worthing FC puts focus on mental health as supporters association partners with suicide prevention charity Olly’s Future

The charity, founded by Worthing mum Ann Feloy, has been announced as Worthing FC Supporters Association's chosen charity of the year and a fundraising day was held on Saturday, October 31.

Nearly 4,000 fans attended the game against Sutton United at Woodside Road and representatives of Olly’s Future were there with collection buckets. The charity also received a split of the match-day raffle, bringing the total raised to £870.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Ann set up the charity in memory of her son Oliver Hare, who took his own life on February 14, 2017, just before his 23rd birthday. Its work includes delivering training worldwide to equip people with the skills to spot signs of someone who may be thinking of suicide and have a conversation that could help save their life.

Ann said: “We're delighted Worthing FC has chosen Olly's Future as its charity of the year. My son Oliver loved playing all kinds of sports, from football and rugby to tennis and squash.

“It's a local club being bold enough to get behind the message that suicide prevention is everyone's business, and particularly football where the majority of spectators are men.

“This is what the recent The Royal Foundation of the Prince and Princess of Wales' campaign On Your Side, hosted by Jake Mills Hub of Hope and fronted by Harry Kane, looks like on the ground.

“We all know the facts that three quarters of suicides are by men and that suicide is the biggest killer of men under 50. Supporting our suicide prevention charity goes a long way to reaching that vital target audience and we'll be working with the club to ensure we can help save lives from suicide together.

“However, this comes at a time when the town is in shock about the closure of its Worthing Samaritans branch, which has left volunteers reeling. I've spoken to many in the past week, since they were told of the closure of their premises in an efficiency drive.

“Local volunteers tell me they are being asked to work from home, which they feel is not tenable as it's vital for their own well-being to be with colleagues, or else drive to Brighton to carry out their shifts.

“For every step forward in suicide prevention, there seems to be two steps back. The Samaritans are closing numerous premises around the country - Worthing is not alone.”

The Rebels will be working with Olly’s Future throughout the coming season and the supporters association, run by Natalie Lunn, will be donating some of the proceeds from away match coach travel to the charity.

Natalie said: “I work as a nurse and know how difficult it is to access care for physical health let alone mental health. So when we were looking for a charity to support, I went online and found Olly’s Future, which is based locally.

“I have sons myself and some of their formative years were during Covid and I know how difficult it can be for young people. So,it is great to be able to contribute to a charity doing such valuable work.”

The club produced an enamel badge, linking the Love and Light logo of Olly’s Future with the team, for the fundraising day and this proved popular with supporters.

James Davies, Olly’s Future chief executive, has followed non-league football most of his life and he was part of the fundraising team on the day.

He said: “For us it is excellent to have such a relationship with a club which shows how much it cares about the issue of suicide.

“You see more than 3,000 people gathered together in one space and this offers a chance to open up about issues which are concerning them. They are with friends and are experiencing a sense of belonging as they get together to support the team.

“Non-league teams may not have the resources and the large fan-base of the bigger clubs, but they are very obviously rooted in towns such as Worthing and play a major part in the community. Tickets are also affordable in ways that premiership attendance is not for many people.”

His own recent personal experience has shown how much going to watch a match can mean to people who might otherwise be feeling isolated.

James explained: “I recently lost my grandmother and my grandfather, aged 87, had been her carer in her last years. He has started going each week to watch both Portland United and Weymouth matches along with other family members, which stops him just being at home and alone with his thoughts, and when I went with him, he really did open up about his feelings.”

#1895. Late push can’t save Lewes as Dartford win on fiery night at the Pan

In a clash of two high-flying teams in the Isthmian Premier Division table, a swift first-half double from Dartford proved decisive at The Dripping Pan.

Ben Greenhalgh’s powerful strike and Dan Smith’s opportune rebound punished two moments of Lewes disorganisation before the half hour. While the Rooks responded well, they struggled to break down a stubborn Darts backline and had to wait until the 82nd minute for a scorching Brian Garzon goal.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Despite pouring everyone forward late on, this left too little time to secure an all-important equaliser.

Lewes began the evening with three changes to their starting XI, with Ben Mundele, Tyler Christian-Law and Danny Bassett returning in place of Tyler Cox, Kurtis Cumberbatch and Bobby Unwin.

After a spectacular entrance featuring Southover Bonfire Society’s torches and fireworks, the game itself proved more of a slow burner.

Both teams used the opening stages to feel one another out, and the first chance came after almost 15 minutes, when an unmarked Charlie Walker headed Danny Bassett’s delivery over the bar. Lewes then lost defender Harry Mills to an awkward injury, forcing them into a reshuffle as Olly Hamstead came on.

Just a minute later, Dartford seized upon this as player-manager Greenhalgh found space on the edge of the box for a sharp left-footed strike into the top left corner. The Rooks were almost immediately level when Mundele connected with Christian-Law in the box, but the midfielder couldn’t get a clean connection on his effort.

Heading back up the other end, Dartford then doubled their advantage as an initial shot was saved by Louis Rogers and the Lewes defence was too slow to react as Smith drilled home. The Rooks stabilised and began to gather some momentum before half-time.

Their best chance came as Ryan Gondoh drove forward and found Charlie Walker, who in turn located Garzon for a powerful drive stopped by defender Ben Swift. After what was surely a frank discussion at the break, Lewes returned with much more of the ball in the second half.

Dartford proved a tough nut to crack, with their fluid system quick to close down any gaps and continuing to threaten on the counter. Charlie Walker won a free-kick 20 yards from goal in the 55th minute but sent the set piece over the crossbar.

This spell proved Lewes needed a change of system, and with Tyler Cox replacing Mundele, the Rooks soon moved to a back three. It did the trick of freeing up Cox and Jack Enkh, who posed regular problems for the visiting defence.

With Bassett and Walker also taken off, the Rooks opted for a system featuring multiple runners but no clear central target. Chances started to flow at both ends, with Enkh crashing a shot into the side-netting, Garzon having an effort saved by Ryan Sandford and Hamstead clearing the danger at the other end as Max Fiddes went clean through.

Gondoh was then foiled by Sandford as his shot took a deflection off George Whitefield.

In the 82nd minute, Lewes found their breakthrough as Gondoh drove down the right and found Garzon on the edge of the box, where he fizzed a low shot past Sandford. The Rooks pushed hard in the remaining minutes, but Dartford dropped deep and closed off any angles towards goal.

The best remaining chance fell to Tyrese Owen in an added-time pinball in the box, as his audacious backheel was hooked away. Lewes therefore tasted defeat at home for just the second time this season, while a five-match unbeaten run in October came to an end.

The Rooks are 4th in the table after 15 games and now head to 12th-placed Dulwich Hamlet this weekend. Kick-off is 3pm at Champion Hill on Saturday.

Lewes FC: Rogers; Mundele (Cox, 63’), Mills (Hamstead, 21’), Spinks, Enkh; Christian-Law, Owen; Gondoh, Garzon, Bassett (Fisher, 70’); Walker (Unwin, 72’)

Tenerife centre-forward De Miguel sustained severe head and chest injuries following a heavy collision with Andorra goalkeeper Owono, who was subsequently shown a red card for the challenge.

Owono had raced out of his his goal in an attempt to clear the ball when the deadly coming together occurred in the closing stages of Monday’s Spanish second-division contest.

It quickly became apparent that De Miguel required urgent medical attention and while the striker’s condition was described as ‘stable but serious’ after he was carried from the field and taken to hospital, his condition quickly deteriorated.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

A heartbreaking statement on Tenerife’s social media pages on Tuesday morning confirmed that De Miguel has succumbed to his injuries, devastating news that has rocked the footballing world to its core.

Players and organisations have united in support of De Miguel’s friends and family in the hours that have followed, with heartfelt tributes shared and moments of silence observed across the globe.

Meanwhile, the Spanish FA postponed all Copa del Rey and Copa de la Reina matches that were scheduled to take place on Tuesday to allow for time to ‘grieve over this sad loss’.

It has also been announced that Tenerife’s Segunda Division clash with Granada – which had been due to kick off on Saturday – will be moved to a later date.

‘The new date for the match is pending confirmation. The club reiterates its deepest condolences to the loved ones of Jesus de Miguel, as well as to the entire CD Tenerife family, sending them all strength and encouragement in these difficult times.’

Con el corazón encogido. Impresiona esto. Cientos de aficionados están despidiendo en estos momentos a Jesús de Miguel junto a la puerta 9 del Heliodoro. #jesusdemiguel pic.twitter.com/9aoHdlAh87

Reuters reported on Tuesday that police in Spain had launched an investigation for possible involuntary manslaughter in the wake of De Miguel’s death.

However, criminal proceedings against Andorra shot-stopper Owono are ‘very unlikely’, according to Santa Cruz de Tenerife chief prosecutor Jose Luis Sanchez-Jauregui.

🖤 A moment of silence in memory of @CDTOficial forward Jesús de Miguel Alameda and the victims of last week’s train accident in Spain. pic.twitter.com/o1e4bQRX3E

Owono is yet to make a public statement in relation to the incident and Venancio Tomas Ndong Micha, the president of the Equatorial Guinean Football Federation, has said the 25-year-old was ‘experiencing profound distress and anguish’ following the news of De Miguel’s death.

Spanish radio station COPE reported that a section of supporters inside the Heliodoro Rodriguez Lopez stadium had yelled ‘murderer’ at Owono, appearing to blame the goalkeeper for the tragic circumstances that played out.

But Andorra defender Spatz, who helped carry De Miguel off the pitch on a stretcher, took to Instagram to defend Owono on Tuesday night, insisting his team-mate would ‘never intentionally hurt anyone’.

‘There are moments when football stops making sense. Moments that stay with you forever and make you realise just how fragile life can be. What we have experienced is something none of us will ever forget. A tragedy that has left us completely heartbroken, speechless and with a sadness that is difficult to put into words,’ Spatz wrote.

‘First of all, I would like to express my most sincere condolences and send all my love to the family, friends and loved ones of Jesus, as well as to the entire Chicharrera fanbase and the football community.

‘Since yesterday, the entire FC Andorra squad has been shocked, devastated and deeply affected by what has happened. It is a tragedy that we could never have imagined experiencing on a football pitch.

‘I would also like to say a few words about my team-mate, goalkeeper and friend, who has been deeply affected by what happened. Those of us who know him know what kind of person he is, how much he is suffering at this moment, and that he would never intentionally hurt anyone.

‘In football, accidents happen, but nobody could ever imagine that one of them could lead to such tragic consequences.’

The Andorra centre-back added: ‘Today, football doesn’t matter. All that matters is standing together in grief, showing the utmost respect and sending all our strength to the family and everyone suffering from this terrible loss.

‘Rest in peace, Demi. [broken heart emoji].’

A separate message on Andorra’s official website read: ‘We are deeply moved by the death of Jesus de Miguel. The first thing we want to do is extend our most sincere condolences to his family, CD Tenerife, and all those close to him.

‘We know that no words can ease such pain, but we want them to know that we stand by their side and deeply share their sadness.

‘We also want to extend all our support to CD Tenerife, its players, its technical staff, its workers, and its fans. We are deeply affected by what has happened and share the pain the club is experiencing. From the very first moment, we have been in contact with them and are at their disposal for anything they may need.

‘Likewise, we are in contact with LaLiga, the Government of Andorra, and the relevant organizations to offer all our collaboration and the necessary support during these very difficult times. We have also requested the postponement of the next match against RCD Mallorca, as we believe these are moments of profound grief in which respect and support for all those affected must prevail.

‘What has happened has had a great emotional impact on our players, the technical staff, and everyone who is part of FC Andorra. These are especially tough times for everyone, and we want to ensure that no one has to face them alone. For this reason, the club is providing psychological support to all those who need it.

‘We are a team, on and off the field. Now more than ever, we must stand together, support each other, and take care of one another.

‘All of football and all of sports are in mourning. These are moments of profound sadness in which we must remain united, support those who need it most, and show the utmost respect.

‘Our most sincere condolences to Jesús’s family and to everyone at CD Tenerife. Rest in peace, Jesus.’

#1893. Horsham FC boss hails biggest National League South victory to date – but cup win is forgettable

The ruthless Hornets served up a Halloween treat for their supporters as they stormed to a 5-0 win at Farnborough on Saturday.

The visitors led 2-0 at half-time through James Hammond’s free kick and Greg Luer’s tidy finish. George Cox’s rocket, Reece Myles-Meekums’ close-range effort and Harvey Sparks’ ferocious strike sealed Horsham’s biggest step two win in the second half.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

The thumping victory moved the Hornets up to tenth – and within three points of the play-off places – going into this Saturday’s home clash with AFC Totton.

Di Paola told us: “We’ve had a Jekyll & Hyde week really, but Saturday was brilliant. We played really, really well. There were some excellent goals and it was a brilliant performance.

“Even when they put us under the cosh at times, we defended really well and looked like a good unit. Collectively there were some really good performances.

“It was a much-needed win against one of the teams near us. It’s amazing because if you get the second or third goal, with the way we play, then the game becomes quite easy. What’s been the challenge in this league, and will continue to be the challenge, is getting those second or third goals to take the game away from the opposition.

“We had such good support on Saturday. It’s such a nice thing when you have a good performance and that level of support. I could see how happy they were.”

Horsham went ahead at Farnborough in the 43rd minute courtesy of a delicious Hammond free-kick. Luer then added the Hornets’ second on the stroke of half-time after good work from Charlie Hester-Cook to win the ball deep in Farnborough territory.

Cox made it three with a ferocious 25-yard piledriver on 74 minutes before Myles-Meekums poked home from close-range for Horsham’s fourth four minutes later.

Substitute Sparks then added the icing on the cake in second half stoppage time to confirm the Hornets’ biggest ever National League South win.

And Di Paola revealed Sparks’ goal was his pick of the bunch.

He added: “Harvey’s was my favourite just because of the way we pulled them all over the pitch and then attacked the space. That’s the kind of thing you look at and work on in training.

“It doesn’t always happen like that. It was nice to pull them all the way back into our half, go all the way back through the pitch, come outside where we’ve created space and go and score. It was a good way to win the game.

“The bundled goal was a bit different, but it was a good day at the office really.”

But Horsham were far less fluent away to SCFL Premier outfit Pagham in the Sussex Senior Cup on Tuesday evening.

A heavily-rotated Hornets team left it late to edge past the Lions 1-0, Ashley Nadesan tapping home with just three minutes remaining after Pagham’s goalkeeper dropped a high-hanging cross at his feet.

Di Paola said: “The highlight for me was that the game finished. It was an awful game of football played on an awful pitch.

“The pitch levelled the game, which meant we couldn’t play any real football. That’s not an insult to Pagham. When I was at East Preston, me and another guy used to jump on the mower and try and make the pitch as nice as possible back in the day. At Climping, when it got to October and the pitch was like a cow field. I’m not being a snob, I just think it’s very difficult to do anything on a bad pitch.

“There were a fair few performances that I was really unhappy with – and I said that to the boys at half-time. I thought some of them were bad – not because we haven’t gone and rattled 20 past them, but because of the general application and lack of desire.

“We mixed and matched it. You have to demonstrate why you’re not playing. It doesn’t mean you have to play well, you need to have the right attitude.

“People don’t need to impress me with goals or unbelievable play, I want players to give everything. I felt in the first half, in particular, we were slow in everything we did. We didn’t press, we didn’t sprint, we played within ourselves.

“A few didn’t do themselves any favours in the first half. In the second, we were slightly better. I thought Niall McManus was good, I thought Jack Brivio had a good second half, but not many of them came out with a great deal of credit.

“I’m glad we got through and got a goal late on. It was a tough night, frustrating night, an awful game of football. Anyone who came to watch that just didn’t see any real quality in the whole game.”

The victory at Pagham was Di Paola’s 300th as Horsham manager – but the boss was ambivalent about the milestone.

He added: “When I get to 1,000 games I will be quite proud of that one. I think that could be next season if we carry on, which I think is quite an achievement – but those kinds of milestones don’t really mean anything to be honest. I didn’t know anything about it.

“But that’s 300 good days in 12 years. We’ve almost got a year of good days!

“I personally don’t really look at stuff like that. It doesn’t make a lot of difference to me. When we get to the 1,000th game I will crack open a cider and wonder what I’ve done with my life!”

The Hornets have no fresh injury concerns ahead of Saturday’s home encounter with 18th-placed AFC Totton.
