#1819. When Arsenal can qualify for Champions League knockout phase after Slavia Prague win

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Arsenal took a giant step towards sealing qualification for the Champions League knockout phase with victory over Slavia Prague on Wednesday night.

Noni Madueke and Viktor Gyokeres had the Gunners in cruise control at half time at the Fortuna Arena, the latter producing, arguably, his best all-round performance since arriving from Sporting last summer.

Arsenal had chances to extend their lead through Eberechi Eze and Mikel Merino, but were almost punished for such profligacy.

As Slavia head coach Jindrich Trpisovsky tinkered with his system during the interval, a double substitution - combined with the Gunners not matching the high standards they set in the opening 45 minutes - meant the second half told a different story.

Gabriel was forced into a desperate clearance under his own bar, David Raya produced one sensational save to tip a header onto the post and Arsenal survived a VAR check for a Slavia Prague penalty.

Wiktor Nowak was able to pull a goal back for the hosts in second half stoppage time, but the Gunners held on to move up to third in the 36-team Champions League table following defeats for Liverpool and Real Betis.

It is now three wins and a draw for Arsenal from their opening four games in this season’s league phase, and victory in Prague should be enough to avoid an early elimination from the competition.

In fact, the result sees the Gunners move back to within two points of holders Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid - the only two sides with perfect winning records at the halfway stage.

Arsenal still have to play Jose Mourinho’s side, but next welcome Borussia Dortmund to the Emirates Stadium before rounding off the league phase against Real Betis and Sabah in the new year.

Of course, in this new Champions League format, the luxury a top-eight finish brings is automatic qualification to the last 16 as well as avoiding two extra games in the play-off round for the knockout phase.

As things currently stand, Mikel Arteta's side still have plenty of work ahead to ensure they finish in the top eight for a third consecutive season.

Jindrich Trpisovsky issues Arsenal verdict after Champions League defeat

Arsenal dealt new injury worry as Mikel Arteta forced into substitution

Mikel Arteta concerned by Arsenal's second half in win over Slavia Prague

However, finishing in the top 24 is already within reach - based on the points totals from the last two league phase campaigns.

In 2024-25, Club Brugge qualified with 11 points, while nine points were enough for Benfica to scrape through in dramatic fashion 2025-26.

Arsenal already have 10 points from a possible 12. Therefore they can, perhaps, guarantee a place in this season’s Champions League knockout phase with victory over Dortmund on November 24 before targeting a bye into the round of 16.

#1818. Dowman weaves his magic and new signing shines as Arsenal hit ground running

Teenage sensation Max Dowman was the star of Arsenal’s first pre-season match, as he scored one goal and assisted another in a 4-1 victory over Girona.

Dowman, 16, was joined on the scoresheet by new signing Christos Tzolis, who struck with a low effort in his first game since his £34m move from Belgian side Club Brugge.

Established attackers Kai Havertz and Gabriel Jesus also scored for the Premier League champions, who were largely comfortable against opposition from the Spanish second tier.

Here are four things Telegraph Sport learnt from the match:

It was this time last year that Dowman first announced his remarkable talent to the wider world. Then only 15, he sparkled in pre-season and made it clear to Mikel Arteta that he was ready to impact matches at the highest level.

A year on, Dowman is now an established first-team player. He is the youngest ever Premier League winner and the competition’s youngest ever scorer, and he looks set to make even more of a mark this season.

In this friendly against Girona, Dowman created Arsenal’s opening goal with a gorgeous defence-splitting pass for Havertz. He did so after receiving the ball under pressure and spinning into space. Dowman then scored Arsenal’s third with a powerful low drive from the edge of the box.

Dowman is in competition with Bukayo Saka and Noni Madueke for a place on the right wing, which means this summer represents a huge opportunity for the teenager. After playing for England at the World Cup, Saka and Madueke will both miss most of pre-season.

Dowman, therefore, has a serious chance of going into the new campaign as the starting right-winger. The Community Shield on August 16 must be a target in his mind.

“We know what he’s capable of doing,” Arteta said. “We want to be more consistent in terms of the performances and the actions that he can deliver, but I think today he had a really good game.”

Arsenal are close to completing a deal for Newcastle United captain Bruno Guimarães but, for now, their only outfield signing of the summer has been Tzolis. This was the Greek winger’s first match in front of supporters and he immediately demonstrated why Arsenal were willing to pay £34m to buy him from Club Brugge.

With Tzolis, it is all about the final product. Goals and assists. He struck 22 times for Club Brugge last season, and registered 29 assists.

How did he produce such impressive numbers? The answer could be seen in his first-half goal against Girona. Receiving the ball on the left wing, Tzolis quickly accelerated towards the penalty area and unleashed a low shot. It was perhaps a more direct approach than Arsenal would usually have seen from Leandro Trossard, the player Tzolis has replaced, and it caught Girona off-guard as the ball deflected into the net.

“I’m very pleased with him,” Arteta said. “First of all, the way he has adapted to the club, to the team. The connection he’s already generating with the boys. I think you’re going to love the player.

“A player who’s very direct. He’s got the goal between the eyes. He has a lot of similarities with Leo [Trossard] in a lot of the things that he can do and the spaces he can occupy. And then the work rate that he has... He’s a boy that comes with so much hunger. He wants to prove himself, it’s a dream for him. And we are here to help him.”

Havertz was one of the few Arsenal players who benefited from playing at the World Cup. His injury issues mean that, unlike most of his team-mates, he did not end the 2025-26 season in a state of exhaustion.

After returning to the pitch in the spring, Havertz enjoyed an impressive end to the campaign for Arsenal. He then performed well at the World Cup, scoring three goals for Germany.

He remains one of Arteta’s favourite players, not least because of his versatility. He started in attack in the crucial end-of-season games in May, but played in midfield against Girona. His low finish, from Dowman’s pass, represented his eighth goal in his last 12 matches for club and country.

Girona’s goal, scored by Arnau Martínez, was perhaps the only alarming moment of this comfortable pre-season victory. Martínez was unmarked from a left-wing corner when he powered a header into Arsenal’s net.

For a group of players who pride themselves on their set-piece prowess, this was a disappointing moment. It also perhaps showed Arsenal’s reliance on their two first-choice centre-backs, William Saliba and Gabriel Magalhães, when they are defending crosses into their box.

Gabriel arrived at Arsenal’s pre-season training camp a few days ago, so he should be in good shape by the start of the new campaign. Saliba, though, will be missing for months with a back problem.

Without Saliba’s height and power, will Arsenal be as effective from set-pieces in the opening chunk of the campaign? Coventry City, Arsenal’s opponents on the first night of the season, will undoubtedly look to test the champions in these situations.

The reigning Premier League champions are handed the Costa Brava Trophy, which is half-heartedly lifted into the air by White. There will be far bigger trophies on offer to Arsenal in the upcoming campaign.

Arsenal have cruised to a routine 4-1 win over Girona, with Havertz, Tzolis, Dowman and Gabriel Jesus all finding the net. Arteta will be delighted with his side’s professionalism and ruthlessness.

Meslier takes too long on his goal kick, gifting a corner to Girona. However, the delivery from the hosts is so poor as it flies harmlessly out of play. That sums up Girona’s difficult evening.

There is another round of substitutions for both sides.

Two more changes in the offing...↩️ Jesus, Copley🔛 Agustien, Julienne🔴 1-4 🔵 (85) pic.twitter.com/3qt6N63qzq

🔁 Últim canvi al Girona:➡️ Stuani⬅️ Pyshchur

Once again, Meslier makes a pivotal stop on his Arsenal debut. Martin clips an exquisite pass over Arsenal’s defence to the onrushing Ruiz, who is through on goal. The striker takes the chance first time, but Meslier is there to make another crucial save.

Arsenal’s makeshift line-up, which is full of Hale End graduates, is holding firm, with Girona evidently struggling for attacking inspiration. If Arsenal can see out this victory without any injuries, then it would have panned out exactly how Arteta would have wanted.

Girona carelessly give possession away in defence, allowing Nelson to dribble towards the penalty area. The winger floats a cross into the box, which is met by O’Neill, but the forward’s lofted header hits the top of the bar.

There is cooling break in this second half to give both sets of players a quick breather. It’s been a professional performance from Arsenal, who now have various academy prospects on the pitch. Can any of them follow in Dowman’s footsteps and make an eye-catching impression in this match?

Girona make another flurry of changes, giving the youngsters from the club’s academy an opportunity to impress.

🔁 Més canvis al Girona:➡️ Gibert, Holmes, Izan, Misehouy i Jastin⬅️ Arnau, Fran Beltrán, Francés, Bryan i Minsu pic.twitter.com/fb7aVKloFx

Kabia gets to the byline and intelligently pulls a cross back to Gabriel Jesus, who curls a first-time strike narrowly wide of the far post as Arsenal search for a fifth goal.

Meslier showcases his magnificent reflexes, making a world class save to deny the recently-introduced Ruiz from close-range after he latched onto Martinez’s dangerous delivery.

Both sides make numerous changes to their line-ups to manage minutes and give the younger players some game time.

A flurry of substitutions...↩️ Arrizabalaga, White, Tzolis, Nwaneri, Dowman, Vieira, Mosquera, Calafiori, Lewis-Skelly🔛 Meslier, Nelson, Kabia, Ibrahim, Copley, Clarke, O'Neill, Harriman-Annous, Ogunnaike🔴 1-4 🔵 (61) pic.twitter.com/GDXL0JRzkT

Dowman was the breakout star of pre-season last year, when he was only 15, and he has started this campaign in similarly thrilling fashion. One assist, one goal. As you would expect, he looks bigger and stronger.

Arsenal overturn the ball in midfield and it breaks perfectly into the Brazilian’s path. Gabriel Jesus is one-on-one and makes no mistake, applying a devastating finish to make it 4-1 and put the result beyond any doubt.

The 16-year-old prodigy now has a goal and an assist. Dowman picks up the ball in the right attacking pocket, palms off Moreno, who bizarrely throws himself to the ground holding his face, before firing a resounding effort into the bottom corner. He’s such a talented footballer and looks at home in Arsenal’s first team.

Out of nothing, Girona have pulled a goal back. Kim whips a corner into the box, with the unmarked Martinez slamming a magnificent header into the top corner, leaving Kepa rooted to the spot. Arteta will be furious with his side’s complacency there.

🎯 El gol d'Arnau pic.twitter.com/Op6oX3LBzK

The team known as “Set Piece FC” looked alarmingly vulnerable at that Girona corner. Perhaps this is simply the reality of life without William Saliba and Gabriel Magalhaes. The good news for Arsenal is that Gabriel is back with the squad and should be ready to go for the start of the campaign. The bad news is that Saliba’s back injury will rule him out for months. Will that lead to more sustained vulnerability over the opening chunk of the season?

Girona have sent a host of players out to warm up. They’re playing in their fourth pre-season match, with their league campaign due to start on August 16 against Leganes.

We are back under way for the second half.

That was a straightforward half for Arsenal. Arteta will be pleased with Havertz’s showing in his 33 minutes on the pitch. After missing so much of last season through injury, it has been a good summer for Havertz so far. He scored three goals in Arsenal’s final six games of 2025/26, and then netted four times for Germany in June.

The 2009-born playmaker was Arsenal’s standout player in that first half. Dowman’s confidence and class on the ball has been brilliant, with his expertly-crafted assist for Havertz’s opener an obvious highlight.

Arsenal are in complete control here in Spain thanks to first-half strikes from Havertz and Tzolis.

A dominant first-half display in Girona 🙌 pic.twitter.com/ZprG2xLYyj

Dowman dribbles into the penalty area with ease, drifting past a couple of defenders before he is apprehended by Moreno. He goes down, but there is very little in the challenge.

Arsenal are in cruise control here. Girona are chasing shadows. Unsurprisingly, there’s a real gulf in class and quality between the two sides.

Once again, Dowman dances away from Moreno. The youngster sets up White with a reverse pass, but the Arsenal captain’s disappointing cross drifts out for a goal kick.

Tzolis registered 22 goals and 29 assists for Club Brugge last season. He is an end-product machine, and that goal was a little indication of how he racks up such eye-watering numbers. After receiving possession on the left wing, he was so quick to shift the ball onto his right foot and fire the shot at goal. He describes himself as a “direct” player and that was evidence of it.

There are three early changes for Arsenal, with Gyokeres, Havertz and Hincapie taken off for Gabriel Jesus, Vieira and Salmon.

We're making a triple substitution...↩️ Havertz, Hincapie, Gyokeres🔛 Vieira, Salmon, Jesus🔴 0-2 🔵 (32) pic.twitter.com/NtpnUsfAY6

The new winger is one-on-one with Martinez and darts inside, before firing a low effort into the bottom corner. It took a slight deflection, leaving Gazzaniga with no chance. Tzolis has looked lively and slotted into Arsenal’s attack seamlessly so far.

Tzolis is slipped into the penalty area from his left-wing berth, but instead of shooting, he tries to find Gyokeres with a pass. Girona surround the Swede before Dowman’s follow-up strike is blocked.

Since their goal, Arsenal have assumed real authority of this encounter and look like the far superior side.

Girona captain Martinez slams a powerful long-range effort at goal, but it fizzes wide of the bottom corner. Kepa seemed to have it covered regardless.

Arsenal are hunting for a second, with Lewis-Skelly picking out Havertz with a floated pass. The former Chelsea man is inches away from teeing up Gyokeres for a second, but Gazzaniga is there to make a goal-saving interception. Dowman has also been heavily involved in these early stages, providing the assist for Havertz’s opener.

After his extraordinary breakthrough campaign last year, Max Dowman has a huge opportunity this summer. With England wingers Bukayo Saka and Noni Madueke not returning until later in pre-season, Dowman has a chance to take ownership of the right wing position ahead of the Community Shield. His assist for Kai Havertz, a lovely measured pass after an excellent piece of skill in midfield, was a sign that Dowman means business.

Dowman drifts inside and pops up in the right channel, wriggling past Moreno, before threading a delightful pass through to Havertz. One-on-one, the German calmly slots a close-range effort into the bottom corner, giving Arsenal a well-deserved lead. So much credit must go to Dowman, who has started this game excellently.

Girona have some sustained possession to take the sting out of the game then burst into Arsenal’s penalty area, with the ball attempted to be pulled back to Van De Beek. The visitors have good numbers defending and comfortably deal with the danger.

Tzolis floats a free kick into the box, which Gyokeres meets at the back post. The striker directs the ball back across goal towards Calafiori, whose close-range header is caught by Gazzaniga.

It also appears that Havertz and Nwaneri have been tasked with quite free-roaming attacking midfield roles, with Lewis-Skelly positioned as a one-man holding pivot. It’s a strong but experimental line-up from Arteta.

After suffering an injury at the end of last season and missing the World Cup, White returns to action here this evening and wears the armband. He will look to support Dowman, who appears to be starting on the right wing.

It’s been a confident start from Arsenal, who are stroking the ball around in a very assured manner. Havertz looks to pull the strings by firing a low cross towards Gyokeres, but the delivery is scrambled clear by the Girona backline.

White leads Arsenal out onto the pitch to face Girona, who boast the likes of Van de Beek, Gil and Moreno in their starting XI.

Talking earlier this week, Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta sent out a determined message to other clubs by outlining their ambitious transfer plans.

“A lot is happening,” Arteta said. “We all know about the context of this transfer window. From ownership to the board, the sporting director and myself, we know that we want to take this club to a different level.

“That is going to require a better squad, better individuals. We have identified where we have opportunities to grow and to improve and to evolve our game and what is going to be needed to achieve that. Hopefully very soon we can start to put things in a very concrete way.”

Arteta also believes that last season’s Premier League title has served as added motivation for his squad to improve and hit new heights.

“This has to be the start and this has to be the standard,” he said. “Excellence has to be our standard and this has to drive to attack the future. The way we behave daily with more and more determination and ambition, because we’ve shown that we’ve got it. Now we have to show that we belong to this level and we want to increase and take this football club to a different dimension.”

It had been a relatively quiet transfer window for Arsenal, who have recruited just goalkeeper Illan Meslier and winger Christos Tzolis.

However, Arsenal are now moving very bullishly, closing on Newcastle United midfielder Bruno Guimarães, while also targeting Real Madrid’s Vinícius Júnior.

Sam Dean has the full breakdown of a potential deal for the Real Madrid star and how Arsenal are prepared to continue flexing their muscles in the transfer market in what would be one of the biggest moves in Premier League history.

It was January 2025, with Arsenal earning a hard-fought 2-1 comeback victory in the Champions League courtesy of first-half goals from Jorginho and Ethan Nwaneri.

Since this European encounter, Girona have been on a seriously downward trajectory, enduring lowly 16th and 19th finishes in La Liga, with the latter ensuring relegation to the Segunda Division, where they’ll play in the upcoming campaign.

August 5: Arsenal vs Real Betis (Dublin, Ireland)

August 9: Arsenal vs Borussia Dortmund (London, England)

August 12: Arsenal vs Como (London, England)

August 16: Arsenal vs Manchester City (Cardiff, Wales)

Mikel Arteta’s side will then begin their defence of the Premier League title on August 21 when they host newly-promoted Coventry City on August 21.

Arsenal are closing in on one of the statement signings of the summer, with Newcastle United midfielder Bruno Guimarães getting closer to joining the Premier League holders.

This deal means that Christian Norgaard is expected to leave and seal a move to Everton for around £7m.

As previously reported by Telegraph Sport, Guimarães has been Arsenal’s top target for weeks. It is believed that he will cost around £80m.

Sam Dean has the full story via this link.

🔵 𝗧𝗘𝗔𝗠𝙉𝙀𝙒𝙎 🟡©️ White with the armband✨ Nwaneri floating in the middle🆕 Tzolis from the startAnother pre-season test awaits, LIVE on The Arsenal 📺 Presented by @deel 🤝

Hello and welcome to our live coverage for this pre-season friendly between Girona and Arsenal at Estadi Montilivi in Catalonia.

With the transfer speculation surrounding Vinícius Júnior’s and Bruno Guimaraes’ potential moves to Arsenal ramping up, the reigning Premier League champions are in action against Girona as they step up their preparations ahead of the upcoming campaign.

Unlike other Premier League heavyweights, Arsenal have kept their pre-season tour relatively local with a selection of games in Spain, Ireland and England, before they face Manchester City in the FA Community Shield on August 16 at the Millennium Stadium in Cardiff.

Arsenal beat League One side MK Dons 3-0 in a behind-closed-doors friendly on July 25 at the Sobha Realty Training Centre, thanks to goals from Reiss Nelson, Ethan Nwaneri and Ceadach O’Neill.

After featuring in this victory and setting up Nelson for the opener, Christos Tzolis will be looking to continue his positive momentum with his new club, after joining Arsenal for £34m earlier this summer. Many fans will be keeping a close eye on the recently-signed winger given that various core members of last season’s Premier League-winning squad are yet to return from their post-World Cup breaks, having progressed deep in the competition.

Tournament winners David Raya, Martin Zubimendi and Mikel Merino, Norway captain Martin Odegaard, as well as England internationals Bukayo Saka, Declan Rice, Eberechi Eze and Noni Madueke are all missing for this game, while France’s William Saliba is out injured and set for an extended period on the sidelines.

Those who exited the World Cup earlier than the aforementioned players, including Gabriel Magalhaes, Gabriel Martinelli, Piero Hincapie, Kai Havertz, and Viktor Gyokeres, have all joined up with the squad in northern Spain.

Mikel Arteta’s men will play a wounded Girona, who suffered relegation from the top flight of Spanish football last season due to a 19th-place finish.

#1815. Mourinho sends Endrick message amid Arsenal, Villa links

By Naim Beneddra | 05 Nov 2026 15:41

Real Madrid manager Jose Mourinho has admitted his frustration at being unable to give more playing time to some of his talented attackers, while offering fresh insight into Endrick's role amid continued speculation linking the Brazilian with Arsenal and Aston Villa.

The 20-year-old forward has struggled to establish himself in Mourinho's plans this season, despite returning to the Santiago Bernabeu following an impressive loan spell at Lyon.

Endrick was introduced during Wednesday's dramatic 3-2 Champions League victory over AEK Athens, featuring on the right flank as Madrid recovered from a 2-1 deficit to maintain their perfect record in the competition.

After the match, Mourinho acknowledged the difficulty of managing a squad containing so many high-quality players, while highlighting the particular threat Endrick offers against tired defenders.

His comments come at a time when the youngster's limited opportunities have once again raised questions about whether a January departure could be beneficial to his development.

Speaking after Federico Valverde's stoppage-time winner in Athens, Mourinho conceded that he found it difficult to leave talented players out of his team.

"It frustrates me for all those who are not playing because everyone deserves to play," the Portuguese coach explained, according to Real Madrid's official website.

Mourinho pointed to the performances of those who have received fewer opportunities as evidence of the considerable depth available to him.

Endrick was among the players singled out for praise, with the former Chelsea and Manchester United manager emphasising the problems his pace and directness can cause opponents.

"I think it's dramatic for a full-back, after playing an hour against someone of quality, to then face Endrick; it's truly complicated," Mourinho added.

The Brazilian replaced Bernardo Silva during the second half against AEK and provided an attacking outlet as Madrid searched for a way back into the contest.

Operating primarily from the right, Endrick created a promising opportunity for Kylian Mbappe late in the match, although the Frenchman's effort was saved.

He also saw a shot blocked during the closing stages, before Valverde secured victory with a powerful strike from outside the penalty area.

Despite those encouraging contributions, Endrick's overall involvement this season remains limited.

The former Palmeiras forward has managed only a handful of appearances and one goal since returning from France, with injuries initially delaying his return to Mourinho's matchday squad.

Competition for attacking positions has subsequently made regular minutes difficult to obtain.

Mbappe remains Madrid's principal centre-forward, while Vinicius Junior, Yan Diomande, Brahim Diaz and Carlos Espi provide further options in the attacking positions.

Mourinho nevertheless insisted that having so many alternatives was a considerable advantage rather than a problem for the team.

"There are many coaches who must look at me with a lot of healthy envy because, when I have problems, I look at the bench and have so many options," he said.

The remarks underline Mourinho's appreciation of Endrick's qualities, although they do not amount to a promise of increased playing time.

Endrick's lack of regular football has attracted attention from several European clubs ahead of the January transfer window.

Arsenal have reportedly made contact with the Brazilian's representatives over a potential move, according to TEAMtalk, with Mikel Arteta's side exploring opportunities to strengthen their attack.

The Gunners are understood to be interested in the forward's versatility and potential, although no agreement has been reported.

Aston Villa have also been linked with Endrick, having previously emerged as a potential destination for another loan spell.

Spanish radio station Cadena SER reported in October that the Birmingham club were among the leading candidates to secure his services, with Lyon and Roma also monitoring developments.

However, Mourinho has repeatedly resisted suggestions that the Brazil international should leave Madrid.

Last month, the Portuguese coach warned clubs interested in Endrick that he was not planning to sanction a January exit, describing the youngster as an important part of his squad.

That position helps explain why Wednesday's comments should not be interpreted as an indication that Madrid are preparing to negotiate his departure.

Endrick demonstrated the benefits of regular football during the second half of last season, scoring eight goals and providing eight assists in 21 appearances under Paulo Fonseca at Lyon.

His performances in France strengthened his reputation and provided valuable experience after a difficult period in Madrid.

Yet Mourinho's latest assessment suggests that he continues to see a specific role for the Brazilian within his own squad, particularly as a substitute capable of exploiting tiring defences.

Real Madrid face Valencia in La Liga on Saturday, with Mourinho confirming that further rotation will be required because of the demanding fixture schedule.

For Arsenal and Aston Villa, the central question remains whether Endrick's opportunities will increase sufficiently before January to justify another six months in Madrid.

Mourinho clearly values the youngster's attacking qualities. Whether that confidence translates into more substantial playing time may ultimately prove more important than his public praise when Endrick's future is reassessed.

#1814. Chelsea injury update: Emi Martinez, Joao Pedro, Maxence Lacroix latest news and return dates

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith

Chelsea have had a few days rest following their 2-0 win over Manchester United, with the focus now on Sunderland.

The Blues will make the trip up north to the Stadium of Light on Sunday afternoon, hoping to sign off for the final international break of 2026 on a positive note.

Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso could be boosted by the return of Emi Martinez for the game and will provide an update on the fitness of star striker Joao Pedro, who has now missed the last three games.

Facing a Sunderland side who are bottom of the Premier League table and trying to balance playing in the Europa League, Chelsea may fancy their chances of avenging the 2-1 loss on the final day of last season - a result that cost them European football.

With that in mind, here is the latest Chelsea injury news and return dates…

Martinez has missed Chelsea's last three games across all competitions after undergoing surgery for a broken jaw sustained upon a collision with Jarrad Branthwaite in the win over Everton last month.

The Argentina international was expected to be sidelined for around six weeks, but Standard Sport reported before the win against Manchester United that there was optimism Martinez could be back fit ahead of schedule, and Alonso confirmed as much in the pre-match press conference.

"Yes, there is a chance. We need to still wait for next week, but let's see how things go," Alonso said in response to being asked if Martinez could return against Sunderland. "But there is a chance."

It would appear that Martinez is on course to be in contention to replace Mike Penders in goal at the Stadium of Light on Sunday afternoon as he was put through his paces at Cobham on Wednesday ahead of Chelsea’s final fixture before the November international break.

The 34-year-old was spotted in the session wearing a protective face mask and will need to do so if selected against Sunderland.

"In case he's ready to play, he will need a face mask probably," Alonso added.

Potential return date: Sunday November 8, vs Sunderland (A)

Joao Pedro was forced to sit out Chelsea’s rare home loss to Tottenham due to picking up a thigh injury in training on the eve of the game.

“He's a key player. We will miss him, but we have to be ready to deal with the injury, and be competitive and try and win with the players we have available. This is the situation.”

Potential return date: Saturday November 21, vs Leeds (H)

Jordan Henderson was a surprise absentee from the Chelsea squad to face Manchester United, despite having played 90 minutes against former club Liverpool in the Carabao Cup three days prior.

The summer signing has forged a decent midfield pairing with Moises Caicedo of late and should be in contention to face another of his old clubs this weekend as any concerns over an injury have already been allayed.

Alonso said Henderson was ill and suffering with a fever last Saturday.

“He's ill," Alonso said of Henderson to TNT Sports. “There's no injury, but he was not feeling well yesterday and today had a fever in the morning, so he was not feeling good enough to come with the team.”

Potential return date: Sunday November 8, vs Sunderland (A)

Chelsea’s influential captain Reece James suffered a knee injury in training at Cobham on his return from another hamstring issue.

After consulting with a specialist, he underwent successful surgery last month that was described as “minor” and Alonso has been reluctant to put a date on his potential return.

However, Standard Sport understands that it is likely to be around three months before James is back in action.

Maxence Lacroix limped off late in the first half of the Carabao Cup penalty shoot-out defeat to Liverpool with a suspected hamstring injury.

Alonso said that Chelsea would need to assess the problem before estimating a recovery time, later admitting that he would be out until after the November international break.

“Max picked up an injury and we expect that he will not be ready before the international break. So he will be a few weeks out,” Alonso said before the win over Manchester United.

Reports have since suggested that Chelsea fear Lacroix, like James, may not play again until the New Year.

Jorrel Hato was a surprise absentee from the Chelsea squad that travelled to Liverpool in the Carabao Cup fourth round and was not available against Manchester United either.

Following the 2-0 win over the Red Devils, Alonso revealed that the Dutchman was battling a back injury.

“How long, we don't know, but he’s not available for tomorrow,” Alonso said. “He has a back problem and he's not feeling okay for tomorrow.”

Potential return date: Sunday November 8, vs Sunderland (A)

Jamie Gittens has yet to make a single Premier League appearance for Chelsea so far this season, with his only two outings to date coming against Luton and Leeds in the Carabao Cup.

The winger has been so unlucky with injuries since arriving in west London from Borussia Dortmund last summer, a trend which continued as he suffered an ankle problem while on international duty with England’s Under-21s last month and needed crutches.

Alonso’s last update confirmed that Gittens was still facing “weeks” on the sidelines, putting him on track to return at some point in November or perhaps even early December.

Potential return date: November or December

In Wednesday’s training session, there was also the rare sighting of forgotten £17million signing Aaron Anselmino.

The 21-year-old has not made a Chelsea senior matchday squad since the Carabao Cup second round win over Luton in August and he has been sidelined with an unspecified injury.

However, he has taken a big step on the road to recovery.

“He’s not available yet,” Alonso revealed last week. “He's had a few things, a few injuries and it still will take a few weeks until he's fully fit and we need to be cautious with him because he has had a few of them so he's still not there.”

Potential return date: November or December

#1813. Callaghan: Nashville ‘hungry for more’ after matching MLS points record

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

BJ Callaghan believes there is still plenty more hunger within his Nashville SC ranks as their record-equalling regular season ends with a trip to FC Cincinnati this weekend.

Nashville produced a stunning comeback to beat the New York Red Bulls 3-2 at GEODIS Park, and in doing so, got themselves up to 74 points.

The Coyotes matched the record for the most points in a single MLS season, equalling Inter Miami's total from the 2024 season when they won the Supporters' Shield.

Julian Hall and Rafael Mosquera had put NYRB two goals to the good, with Cade Cowell also missing a penalty early on before Tim Parker's own goal reduced the deficit.

Nashville were level when Julian Bazan also turned into his own net, with Sam Surridge scoring a 91st-minute winner to ensure his team had the chance to be out on their own with a win against Cincinnati on Decision Day.

"For us, we have continually tried to push and be one of the elite teams not only in the MLS, but also in North America too," Callaghan said after Nashville's win over NYRB.

"I think the body of work that we have shown this season is continually taking steps in that direction.

"It's obviously a big honour for these guys to be in that discussion of being one of the best teams ever to play in the MLS, but I know that they will be hungry for more."

A dream 10 years in the making https://t.co/GKILe7KxaD

— Nashville SC (@NashvilleSC) November 3, 2026

Cincinnati, meanwhile, clinched their spot in the playoffs with a 1-0 win over the Philadelphia Union, with Ayoub Jabbari scoring the only goal in the 70th minute.

It looked as though Cincinnati would miss out on the postseason for the first time in four seasons following a wretched run of form from August until the middle of October.

During that stretch, Pat Noonan's side managed just one win from eight league matches (D2 L5), leaving them adrift of the top nine in the Eastern Conference.

But a four-game unbeaten run since then ensured their spot in the playoffs, and Noonan says the team are hitting form just at the right time.

"It feels that way," Noonan said of the building belief in the squad. "You can always sense these things. I'm sure you're feeling it, the fans are feeling it, people from the outside.

"We know internally what we're capable of and what we haven't been doing at the level that we need to. And all year long, we've been able to produce goals, but we haven't been able to win enough 1-0 games.

"And I think the feeling, the energy, what the group now knows we need to do and feels we can do has been evident recently with how we're playing. And it's not always pretty.

"But the guys have been able to adjust to different ways of defending against the opponent, preparing for the opponent and finding success.

"I like the energy of the group right now, and wins always help that, but I also just like the way we're going about it, and there are a lot of guys contributing and guys coming back into the mix, so I think that makes for a promising final week in preparation for Nashville."

Evander enters the final day of the 2026 regular season with 14 goals and 17 assists.

With one more goal, Evander would join Lionel Messi as the only players in MLS history to record 15+ goals and 15+ assists in three consecutive seasons.

Surridge scored his league-leading seventh game-winning goal of the 2026 season in the win over the weekend.

His 16 game-winners since joining MLS in 2023 are tied with Brian White for third-most in the regular season, behind only Denis Bouanga (24) and Messi (17).

— Nashville SC (@NashvilleSC) November 1, 2026

Nashville recorded a 4-0 win over Cincinnati in August, the largest margin of victory by either team in the history of the series. It was Nashville's third time recording a shutout victory in the fixture, while Cincinnati have kept one clean sheet against Nashville (1-0 win in March 2023).

The Coyotes registered their 22nd win of the season last time out, tying for the most wins in MLS' post-shootout era, joining three others. A win or draw against Cincinnati would give Nashville both the most points and highest points per match in a single season in MLS history.

Cincinnati, meanwhile, have two clean sheets over their last three games, including a 1-0 win last weekend, after going 20 regular-season matches without one prior to that.

The club have not recorded consecutive MLS shutouts in 2026 after having a streak of three straight and two different two-game streaks last season.

#1811. Portsmouth vs Stoke City - prediction, team news, lineups

By Ben Sully | 05 Nov 2026 15:52, Last updated: 05 Nov 2026 20:34

Two in-form sides will face off when Portsmouth welcome Stoke City to Fratton Park for Saturday's Championship encounter.

Pompey head into the weekend in 10th position in the Championship table, while the Potters are in fourth spot and a point adrift of automatic promotion.

Portsmouth share the league's current longest unbeaten run with rivals Southampton after winning four and drawing two of their last six matches.

Pompey continued their impressive run of form with a dramatic 3-1 victory over promotion hopefuls Swansea in Tuesday's clash at Fratton Park.

After seeing his opener cancelled out by Zan Vipotnik's 85th-minute penalty, Terry Devlin put his team back in front in the second minute of stoppage time, shortly before Thomas Waddingham netted in a second straight home game to wrap up all three points.

As a result, Pompey, who have battled relegation in the last two seasons, are sitting just one point adrift from the top eight and four points away from automatic promotion, sparking dreams of ending their 16-year wait for Premier League football.

They will go into Saturday's fixture with hopes of recording four consecutive home league wins for the first time since January 2025.

The fourth win on that occasion came via a 2-1 scoreline against Stoke, which may be a good omen as they look to extend their five-game unbeaten home streak.

Stoke, meanwhile, have lost just one of their last 11 Championship outings, representing a significant improvement from starting the campaign with three consecutive league defeats.

In fact, they have won three of their last four outings since suffering their most recent loss in a home clash against Middlesbrough last month.

The Potters recorded clean sheets in wins against Derby County and Preston North End, either side of a goalless draw against Preston North End.

Mark Robins's side missed out on a fourth consecutive clean sheet in their midweek away clash against Blackburn Rovers, but crucially they left Ewood Park with all three points after claiming a 2-1 victory thanks to a Jack McGlynn effort and an own goal.

That result represented a fourth consecutive win on the road and made it five consecutive away games without defeat since losing to Wolverhampton Wanderers at the end of August.

The Potters enjoyed success on their last trip to Fratton Park in October 2025, when a 70th-minute own goal proved enough to fire them to a 1-0 victory.

Portsmouth remain without Benjamin Arthur, Connor Ogilvie, Mark Kosznovszky, John Swift, Luke Brooke-Smith, Keshi Anderson and Colby Bishop.

Striker Marko Milovanovic has been ruled out of Saturday’s contest after he pulled up with a quad issue in the second half against Swansea.

Midfielder Ilyas Mohamed was also forced off with a calf issue in Tuesday’s win, and while it is believed to be a minor problem, it is unclear whether he will be ready for the weekend.

As for the Potters, they head to Fratton Park without the injured trio of Eric Bocat, Lamine Cisse and Ato Ampah.

Aaron Cresswell and Sam Gallagher are on the verge of returning from injury, but it remains to be seen whether they will prove their fitness in time for Saturday’s away trip.

#1810. 'I told them': Scott Parker reveals team talk that sparked incredible West Ham comeback

New West Ham manager Scott Parker has revealed the half-time team talk that prompted a memorable turnaround away at Cardiff in his first match in charge.

The Hammers trailed 3-0 after only 39 minutes of their latest Championship clash in Wales on Wednesday night, which came just hours after Parker had been officially confirmed as the successor to the sacked Nuno Espirito Santo.

But Parker’s message at the interval hit home as West Ham staged an incredible recovery to snatch an unlikely 3-3 draw.

Goals either side of the hour mark from Divine Mukasa and Arne Engels were followed by Max Kilman’s 82nd-minute strike, cancelling out Jack Moylan’s first-half hat-trick and giving Parker his first point as Hammers boss.

“I came in here at nine o’clock this morning and met the players for the first time, so I didn’t have a lot of input as such,” he said afterwards.

“As you can imagine, it was a difficult half-time talk. I just helped them tactically and told them, ‘OK, this is the way it needs to be now’.

West Ham produce stunning three-goal comeback in Parker's first game in charge

Winter escapes and activities to end the year in style

“Certainly out of possession, we needed to be more aggressive.

“There were tactical changes and substitutions, and we became more front-footed. We took a few more risks.”

It is not the first time that Parker’s half-time speeches have had the desired effect. Bournemouth previously released footage of Parker’s team talk when his former club were locked at 0-0 with automatic promotion rivals Nottingham Forest in the penultimate game of the 2021/22 Championship season.

Bournemouth went on to earn promotion with a 1-0 win via a late Kieffer Moore goal, while Parker has previous with motivating West Ham.

Former team-mate Carlton Cole labelled the midfielder as “inspirational” when he stood up to give a Hammers team talk as a player, with West Ham going from 3-0 down to draw 3-3 with West Brom.

Speaking about his side’s performance against Cardiff, Parker said: “The first half was poor in many aspects. We were very passive and slow with the ball.

“The biggest positive is the team we saw in the second half. That’s what the biggest learning was.

“These boys have come off two defeats. You come to Cardiff away and you’re three-nil down at half-time. I can only imagine what they were feeling.

“They showed a lot of character and that pleased me the most.”

Pre-season promotion favourites West Ham currently sit eighth in the Championship table after 14 games played, five points behind league leaders Middlesbrough.

#1809. Amorim discusses Milan’s consistency, identity and disappointments so far: “We can beat anyone”

Ahead of Thursday’s Europa League game against Ferencvaros, AC Milan head coach Ruben Amorim spoke to the media.

Tomorrow, Milan will be forced to bounce back in Europe with three points. It’s been an up-and-down campaign for them so far, losing to Benfica and Bournemouth, but they grabbed a win against RB Salzburg.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

A top-eight place is not out of the question, but they will have to be perfect for all of their remaining games in the Europa League league phase. In short, it will not be easy, but it’s not impossible.

Tomorrow, the Portuguese is expected to rotate heavily, offering some of his senior players a chance to rest after a very busy October. For example, Strahinja Pavlovic didn’t train today and isn’t expected to start, either.

Speaking alongside Koni De Winter, Amorim addressed the quality of his opponents, rotations and his assessments of the season so far, as MilanNews relays.

The Derby was a good one, but now it’s behind them. Milan needs consistency…

“This is the objective. The Inter game is over and we need to focus on the Europa League. We were very consistent during the derby, but there were games where we weren’t. This is the big step forward we need to take.

“Rotation doesn’t matter, nor the players we field: we need to be a great team. We need to win tomorrow, because it’s crucial to our goal of going all the way in this competition.”

“First of all, the most important match is the next one. We have to be very careful with some players. We have this busy schedule behind us and we can’t afford to lose many players for the next matches, because sometimes, when you don’t want to rotate your squad, you end up with an injury that keeps you out for a month or a month and a half.

“This is the most important match; we’re only thinking about it, but we’ll have to rotate a bit, and all the players are ready to handle the impact of the demands of the game. We have the desire to win the match.

“We’ll be facing a great opponent who has nine points in this competition, a team that hasn’t lost a single game in the league, but our players are ready, and we have a duty to win.”

Why this difference between Serie A and the Europa League?

“But if you look at the games against Benfica, I think we didn’t play our best, despite having more possession. We had some problems with the few chances we gave the opponent, and we conceded goals.

“Then we won a great game in Salzburg and then in Bournemouth. We had a red card, two penalties, and it was our fault. Maignan’s situation didn’t help us fight for the game, and sometimes these dynamics happen at certain times.

“I think we’re not doing very well in Serie A; obviously, we won the last one, but looking at the team and the games, I think we should have more points. So I’m not satisfied in the Europa League, I’m not satisfied in Serie A.

“I think we can do better, but that’s how it goes sometimes. Every game has its own story. But I think we can do better tomorrow and win.”

“They’re a team that’s used to winning, no matter the context. It gives you full confidence in every game. They’re comfortable. They’re doing very well in the league. They play a 4-2-3-1 formation and have a strong identity.

“In midfield, Nagy is very good at building play. They’re comfortable; they come to San Siro with nothing to lose. The responsibility at San Siro is ours: we have to play well and stay focused.

“I told the players that against Inter we did well because we remained humble and attentive to detail: against Ferencvaros, we’ll have to do the same because they’re a very strong team.”

After the Europa League draw, Antonio Cassano said that Milan and Juventus cannot take victory against Ferencvaros for granted…

“Without a doubt. We’re capable of winning every match and losing every match. It depends on our approach, regardless of the opponent. Everyone knows everyone; every player has the tools to understand, and the coaches have the tools to prepare everything as best as possible.

“We can win and lose against anyone; it’s all up to us. And sometimes you also need a little bit of luck.”

Does your AC Milan already have a clear identity? Are we far off?

You often ask me when we’ll reach the top. We’ll never reach the top, even if we win every game. We always have to improve. We already have an identity: we want to dominate games, sometimes we manage to do it, sometimes we don’t.

“Sometimes we change the formation and the defensive phase and nobody even notices. Our identity is to be proactive: we still lack the ability to put opponents in the box to create more chances.

“But we’re playing better, we even manage certain moments better. But there’s still a lot of work to do, especially in the final 30 meters: I have to help my players do that.

On the excellent defensive phase against Inter:

“Inter are a thing of the past. We can show tomorrow that we can defend better. We defended, but with the ball. It allowed us to think better. Details are important: a meter is a meter. We were better than Bologna.

“We were very aggressive on the wings. Koni was exceptional, but if a cross comes in for Thuram, it’s very difficult to defend, so we were more aggressive without the ball to avoid crosses. We have to do the same tomorrow; they are used to winning games.

“When a team consistently wins, there must be a reason, and we have to be ready for tomorrow.”

“We have to give him credit; he’s working really well. He went through a period without playing and was a bit frustrated, but he’s always worked very well. I think he can play this role on the wing. We played with Moreira there once, but against Inter it was Diawara. Same role, different interpretation.

“During the break, against Padova, we tried him at left back: he showed important signs. He’s quick, he’s strong. He’s doing well, he has the potential to improve a lot. Against Inter, we knew how dangerous crosses could be, especially from Inter’s left flank.

“Dimarco didn’t play, but the tactical idea remained the same, and defending crosses with Koni and Pavlovic proved to be a good idea. They almost scored from a cross with Calhanoglu, but I think he’s doing really well.

“He has plenty of room for improvement, and who knows, maybe he’ll start tomorrow.”

“What I was saying about winning games, this is the team’s strength, our identity. I always put the team first, not the individual, even though we have excellent individual players. The Ferencvaros striker is very strong in space: he can play both as a winger and as a forward, and I think he’ll play as a striker against us.

“Nagy is an important player because he understands the game. He knows exactly when to drop back and when to stay high, and I really like that kind of player.

“Add to this the quality of the left-back with his right foot who can cut inside: all these little details define an identity that I really appreciate in this team, and we’ll have to be ready to process all this information to prepare and win the match.

“I repeat: we have three points in this competition and we absolutely must win tomorrow.”

It was the best second half of the entire championship, the one against Inter. I saw the attitude of a great team: authoritative, confident, without taking risks. Should we start again from the second half?

“I think it’s a good point. But you can’t separate the second half from the first; they’re connected. We took the lead in the first half, then we controlled the game that way in the second half. We improved our understanding of the game; we were complete in all areas.

“Maybe we were lacking in putting a few players behind Inter’s midfield: we had good possession, but we can do even better. It’s just one game, anyway. But thinking only about the derby is a small-team mentality: every game is important to us.

“Tomorrow I’ll understand my team better than the derby. I don’t care about the Inter game anymore. Was it nice to win? Yes. But I’m still angry about the Bologna game. Tomorrow we’ll have to be strong to win.”

The Derby showed a side of Cardinale emotional… When will we see her like this too?

“When we win the Scudetto or a major title, maybe I’ll be excited. Until then, it’s just another day. But I didn’t expect to feel this way during the match, and neither did Cardinale. He gave an important interview, saying he supports the coach.

“There was a wonderful feeling in the stadium; he enjoyed this moment and was emotional. He’s American, but when you spend time here, you become a little Italian. However, I won’t be excited until I win something. And when I do win something, I’ll already be thinking about the next Scudetto. I doubt you’ll see me emotional.”

“It’s just one game, anyway. But thinking only about the derby is a small-team mentality: every game is important to us… Was it nice to win? Yes. But I’m still angry about the Bologna game. Tomorrow we’ll have to be strong to win“

#1808. Liverpool injury update: Ryan Gravenberch, Jeremie Frimpong, Hugo Ekitike latest news and return dates

Liverpool suffered a 3-2 defeat by Fenerbahce in the Champions League on Wednesday as their inconsistencies continued.

Transfer news LIVE: Shock Arsenal move, Kroupi twist; Man Utd stunner

Liverpool stunned by Fenerbahce to lose perfect Champions League record

Parker reveals team talk that sparked incredible West Ham comeback

Discover a hidden island paradise in the Indian Ocean

The Reds were beaten by a former club legend in the opposing dugout, Dirk Kuyt, who now manages the Turkish Super Lig side.

Mason Greenwood, Archie Brown and Vedat Muriqi got the goals for the hosts, while Trey Nyoni and Alexander Isak were on target for the visitors.

It was Andoni Iraola’s first European defeat of his tenure in the Liverpool dugout, but he was dealt a further blow on a disappointing evening in Istanbul.

Here is all the latest Liverpool injury news and return dates.

Dutch midfielder Gravenberch has had an injury-hit campaign so far this term.

He missed out on the travelling squad to Turkey as a result of a fracture in his heel, with Iraola providing an update ahead of the trip to the Chobani Stadium.

“I don’t know, it’s a day-to-day thing,” he said.

“It’s a fracture of the heel. It’s about the pain. He has been with some discomfort.

“The other day against Arsenal he was warming up and he was not fully confident. He hasn’t improved since then.

“But it’s going to be something that every day we ask him, every day we see how he is. If he can be available for the weekend, lovely, he would be a very good help for us. But I cannot tell you right now.”

Potential return date: Sunday November 8, vs Crystal Palace (A)

Frimpong picked up a muscle injury playing against Brentford last month, in another lay-off for the full-back since his arrival from Bayer Leverkusen.

The attack-minded right-back is not expected to be back until after the upcoming international break, meaning he will have missed six matches in a row.

On the Dutch international, Iraola said: “Jeremie Frimpong is obviously a new muscle injury and it happened, I think, in the second or third minute he was playing, difficult to predict and we will have to wait until he recovers.

“But it’s going to be difficult, I think, before the [November international] break. We will try but it’s going to be difficult to have him.”

Potential return date: Sunday November 22, vs Manchester United (H)

Leoni signed for Liverpool from Parma last summer in a deal worth around £26million, but a serious knee injury means he has been limited to just one senior appearance so far.

The centre-back made his debut in the Carabao Cup against Southampton in September, but he was stretchered off and it was later confirmed that he had suffered an anterior cruciate ligament tear.

He was expected to miss a full year of action, which has proved to be the case.

He had hoped to have made his comeback for the recent September international break, but that has since been delayed.

“It’s taking more time than we wanted,” Iraola said. “The planning was to train with the team in this past international break [but] probably it’s going to be in the next international break, so we’ve lost one month in the process.

“Giovanni’s injury, I wasn’t here but talking to the medical department, it was not just an ACL – it was a bad injury, a lot of things around the knee were involved apart from the ACL.”

Ekitike has not played since rupturing his Achilles against Paris Saint-Germain in April.

The Frenchman was forced to sit out the end of last season and the World Cup, where it was estimated that he would be out for nine months to a full year.

He was included in Iraola’s squad for the Champions League league phase - which came as a surprise to many - with the hope that he could potentially return for the final two games in January, against Inter Milan and Lens.

The striker is thought to be targeting a comeback before the turn of the year.

Right-back Bradley is another long-term absentee for Liverpool, having suffered a serious knee injury at Arsenal back in January.

The Northern Ireland international suffered bone and ligament damage in that match, which has kept him out for almost a year.

Iraola’s latest comments were positive, indicating that Bradley will soon return to full training.

“[He is] doing very well,” Iraola said. “I think [he is] in a good place. Conor is not so far from training with the group – not like full training but doing some things with the group.

“I think Conor is not very far from starting doing things with us."

It looks as though he could rejoin team training during the November international break.

Potential return date: Wednesday, December 2 vs Sunderland (H)

#1807. Cardiff City vs Burnley - prediction, team news, lineups

By Darren Plant | 05 Nov 2026 15:56

Cardiff City and Burnley square off on Saturday afternoon in what could prove to be a pivotal game in the battle to avoid relegation to League One.

While the Bluebirds sit in 18th position in the Championship table, Burnley are in 22nd spot, already four points adrift of safety.

With eight points from the last five games, Cardiff boss Brian Barry-Murphy can only be delighted with such a return.

The Bluebirds have played Watford, Middlesbrough, Birmingham City, Wolverhampton Wanderers and West Ham United in succession.

However, squandering a three-goal half-time lead against the latter of those teams would have hurt Barry-Murphy, regardless of West Ham benefitting from the arrival of new boss Scott Parker.

In the grand scheme of things, however, Cardiff are five points above the relegation zone and have put together a seven-match unbeaten run at the Cardiff City Stadium.

Trailing 12th place by just three points, the Welsh outfit are still in contention to launch a surprise playoff bid.

At the same time, defeat to Burnley on Saturday would see Cardiff only sit above the relegation zone by two points.

Fabio Celestini has got Burnley back on track with two respectable draws against Portsmouth and Queens Park Rangers.

While the well-travelled Italian knows that the Clarets need to deliver just a second Championship win of the season as soon as possible, there have at least been positives to take from his opening double header.

Burnley have collected five points from their last five away fixtures, arguably an encouraging return for a squad that has struggled to gel.

Nevertheless, if four results - including this one - go against them on Saturday, Burnley would end Saturday seven points adrift of safety.

With Cardiff right-back Perry Ng suffering an injury in the closing stages against West Ham, Ronan Kpakio is in line to deputise.

David Turnbull, Cian Ashford and Joel Colwill will all be considered for recalls due to the quick turnaround after the West Ham fixture.

Gabriel Osho, who has served a three-match ban, could get the nod over Will Fish in the middle of defence.

Barring any fresh injury concerns, Celestini may stick with the Burnley XI from the draw at QPR.

However, Josh Cullen, Aaron Ramsey and Jaydon Banel are all options in midfield and the final third.

Bashir Humphreys, Hannibal Mejbri and Chelsea loanee Dastan Satpaev remain on the sidelines.

Having given up a three-goal lead against West Ham, it is anyone's guess how Cardiff will respond against Burnley. However, they deserve respect for the home record that they have compiled this campaign, leading us to predict a hard-earned victory for the Bluebirds.

#1806. Cifuentes hails Timbers’ togetherness as Decision Day looms

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Marti Cifuentes has hailed his Portland Timbers players for sticking together all season, as they prepare for their MLS Cup Playoff destiny to be decided against Austin FC.

Portland go to Texas for their final game of the regular season on Saturday, sitting eighth in the Western Conference.

The Timbers could still overtake the LA Galaxy and claim an automatic playoff spot, but there is also a chance they could fall out of the wild-card spots – the Colorado Rapids, Seattle Sounders, Real Salt Lake and Minnesota United are all within two points of them.

A victory over Austin – who are 14th in the West and eliminated from playoff contention – would ensure Portland make the postseason regardless of results elsewhere.

But whatever happens, Cifuentes is proud of the way his players have taken to his methods since he took charge in July.

"I think there is always a relationship between confidence and getting results. Usually, the way it works is the better you play, the results will come," he said ahead of the game.

"Then when you're winning, the confidence builds. The credit that I want to give to all those guys is that, during this run, when things were not going our way, the team was growing week by week.

"The guys kept working at exactly the same level, with exactly the same belief. They bought into what we wanted to implement.

"So, it's not just a coach coming here saying, 'We're going to do this', and that's all.

"We've been adjusting certain things during this process, but they are in a good moment now.

"In football and all sports, what you did yesterday is gone. You just have to push on and get the next one."

While Portland registered a crucial 3-1 victory over the Houston Dynamo last time out, Austin went down 4-1 to the Galaxy in their most recent match, with Zan Kolmanic being sent off late on.

Building momentum  All focus shifts to Decision Day in ATX  https://t.co/oTPGfGYN6l

— Portland Timbers (@TimbersFC) November 3, 2026

Austin have conceded 63 goals this season, their most in a single season in club history. At the other end, they have only netted 42 times, with their joint-leading scorers Ramirez and Murto Uzuni scoring nine apiece.

Ramirez will be particularly keen to finish in double figures, having not done so in MLS since his first season with Minnesota United in 2017.

Portland scored twice in the final half-hour against Houston last time out, with Velde netting after the 60-minute mark for the fourth time this year.

Overall, his 11 goals are the most by any Timbers player this campaign, ahead of Kevin Kelsy on nine.

The Portland Timbers have a narrow lead in their all-time series against Austin, with six wins to four (D2).

However, they have only managed one win in the last four encounters between the sides (D1 L2), after going six without losing (W5 D1).

The Timbers have also not lost in Austin since 2021, though only a victory will assure them of a place in the postseason without relying on favours from elsewhere.

They should fancy their chances against Austin, who have only won one of their last eight matches (D2 L5).

Despite that run, Austin have not been held scoreless since September 19, against FC Dallas, finding the net in seven straight games – that could mean there is some Decision-Day drama in store.

#1805. Manchester United co-owners INEOS sack manager as official statement released

INEOS have sacked Lausanne-Sport manager Luka Elsner after just five months at the helm, amid ongoing pressure on Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick.

The Swiss club, which is part-owned by Sir Jim Ratcliffe's INEOS group, confirmed on Tuesday that they had mutually agreed to end their relationship with the 44-year-old.

Elsner was appointed on 1 June but struggled to make an impact, winning eight of his 12 Swiss Super League matches. Lausanne's poor start to the campaign left them bottom of the table, prompting the club to make a change.

A statement read: “After lengthy discussions about the current sporting situation, FC Lausanne-Sport and Luka Elsner have mutually agreed to end their collaboration.”

His departure comes at a difficult time for INEOS at Manchester United, where Carrick is facing scrutiny following a disappointing run of results.

United's supporters have made their frustration with the club's ownership clear in recent weeks, directing criticism towards Ratcliffe and the Glazer family.

Protests continued during Tuesday's Champions League meeting with Roma, when fans threw green and gold balloons on to the pitch in the 21st minute while chanting against the owners.

The atmosphere improved after United produced a second-half comeback to secure a 3-2 victory. Bruno Fernandes scored from the penalty spot before Matheus Cunha struck twice to complete the turnaround.

However, the result is unlikely to remove the pressure on Carrick, who remains under scrutiny as United attempt to improve their domestic form.

The decision to part company with Elsner after such a short period is also likely to attract attention given INEOS' involvement in both clubs.

#1803. Bristol City vs Norwich City - prediction, team news, lineups

By Calum Burrowes | 05 Nov 2026 15:57, Last updated: 05 Nov 2026 16:04

In desperate need of positive results, Bristol City welcome Norwich City to Ashton Gate on Saturday afternoon for a Championship clash.

The Robins suffered their third defeat in five matches on Wednesday, losing 2-1 to Wolverhampton Wanderers, while the Canaries continued their winning streak with a thumping 4-0 victory over Derby County at Pride Park.

There was plenty of optimism surrounding Bristol City following the appointment of Michael Skubala and the investment made during what appeared to be a productive transfer window, but 15 games into his tenure, the former Lincoln City boss is already under pressure and could find his position under threat if results do not improve in the coming weeks.

The early signs at the end of August and start of September were encouraging, with the Robins collecting nine points from a possible nine across a seven-day spell against Portsmouth, Preston North End and Burnley.

However, the South West side have won just twice since then, slipping out of the playoff places and into the bottom half of the table.

Scott Twine's 93rd-minute winner against Bolton Wanderers on Halloween lifted the mood around Ashton Gate, and Bristol City appeared on course to make it back-to-back victories when they entered the final 10 minutes against Wolves with their lead intact, only for a seven-minute brace from Sean Neave to turn the game on its head and condemn Skubala to yet another disappointing result.

Bristol City's main concerns have been their lack of attacking threat and continued struggles at home, with only four sides scoring fewer than the Robins' 16 goals this season and just two teams winning fewer than their two matches at Ashton Gate.

Their attacking problems are clearly a concern for Skubala, who switched to a two-striker system against Stoke City and Bolton Wanderers before reverting to a lone forward for the midweek defeat.

Norwich City, meanwhile, make the trip from East Anglia to Bristol in buoyant spirits, having enjoyed a dramatic turnaround in form that has significantly improved their position in the Championship table following three successive victories.

Wins over Charlton Athletic, Watford and, most recently, Derby County have helped Philippe Clement's side climb from 21st to 12th, leaving them closer to the playoff places than the relegation zone.

The Canaries secured their latest three points in emphatic fashion, travelling to Pride Park in good form and facing a Derby side who had not won since early September.

First-half goals from Anthony Musaba, Paris Maghoma and Darlin Yongwa put Norwich firmly in control before substitute Jovon Makamba came off the bench to add a superb fourth.

Before this winning run, Norwich had scored just twice in their previous 270 minutes of football, but Clement's men have since enjoyed a remarkable upturn in front of goal, finding the net 10 times across their last three matches, with their first clean providing another timely boost.

It was the Canaries' first clean sheet in 24 matches, although their defensive record remains a concern with 24 goals conceded in 14 Championship outings, a total bettered by only a handful of sides, while their recent scoring spree has lifted them to the point where only three teams have a stronger attacking record.

Both teams head into Saturday's encounter level on points and could finish the weekend just one point outside the playoff places.

Although Bristol City came through their midweek encounter without any fresh injury concerns, Skubala still has a number of selection decisions to make.

New signing Sam Tickle was recently dropped in favour of Brad Collins in goal, with the Chelsea academy product starting the last three matches.

However, Collins was at fault for both goals against Wolves and could now find himself relegated to the bench.

Lorent Tolaj was forced off with an injury during the Robins' goalless draw with Stoke City last month and is expected to return in the coming weeks, meaning Saturday's encounter is likely to come too soon for the forward.

Twine, who scored a superb first-half free kick against Wolves, is expected to retain his place in the starting lineup.

Having overseen their best run of the season, Clement will be keen to maintain Norwich's winning momentum for the trip to the South West.

Maghoma and Musaba have scored five goals between them across the last three matches and are expected to feature again in attack, while Mathias Kvistgaarden will continue to lead the line in the absence of Mohamed Toure.

Papa Amadou Diallo and Ali Ahmed remain the only other players unavailable for the Canaries.

Collins; Tanner, McNally, Eissat, Pring; Knight, Williams; Cardines, Tolaj, Twine; Ballard

Both sides head into this encounter level on points but in contrasting form, with Norwich enjoying a three-match winning streak while Bristol City have struggled for consistency.

Nevertheless, the Robins are due a positive result on home soil, and we expect them to end their recent struggles with a closely fought victory on Saturday.

#1802. Cristiano Ronaldo makes bombshell retirement decision after stunning Portugal suspension

Cristiano Ronaldo has retired from international duty with Portugal.

The country’s greatest ever player announced his decision via a video to camera on his social media channels.

Ronaldo scored 146 goals in 234 games for Portugal, becoming the all-time leading scorer in the history of men’s international football.

Between 2003 and 2026, a storied international career delivered three trophies: the European Championship title in France in 2016 and two UEFA Nations League titles, in 2019 and 2025.

Ronaldo said in his social media address that the “time had come” to hand back the No7 shirt but that he had “never felt it belonged to me alone”.

The 41-year-old considered retiring after this summer’s World Cup but was persuaded to stay on by Portuguese FA president Pedro Proenca, a former UEFA referee.

But Ronaldo left Portugal’s training camp on September 30 after a fallout with head coach Jorge Jesus when he was asked to warm up midway through a Nations League game against Norway but was never brought on as a substitute.

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Cristiano Ronaldo has been hailed as "the best player of all time" by the Portuguese Football Federation (FPF) after his international retirement.

Ronaldo called time on his international career on Thursday after a fallout with Portugal head coach Jorge Jesus during the last break.

The 41-year-old holds the Portugal record for appearances (234) and goals (146) after making his debut all the way back in 2003.

He captained Portugal to their first-ever major trophy in 2016, when they won the Euros, before also winning the Nations League in 2019 and 2025.

Ronaldo retires as the only player to have scored at least 10 goals at both the World Cup (11) and the European Championships (14), with the latter figure being a competition record.

The FPF released a statement on Thursday, in which they revealed a farewell will be planned for the Portugal great.

The statement read: "The Portuguese Football Federation expresses its deepest and most enduring gratitude to its eternal captain, Cristiano Ronaldo, who announced his definitive retirement from the National Team.

#1799. Cristiano Ronaldo statement in full after stunning retirement decision

Cristiano Ronaldo confirmed that he would retire from international football in a shock announcement on Tuesday.

The 41-year-old calls time on his illustrious 23-year career playing for his country, where he scored 146 goals in 234 games, becoming the all-time leading scorer in the history of men’s international football.

He lifted the European Championships in 2016, and he also won two Nations League titles in 2019 and 2025.

At last summer’s World Cup, the striker could not stop his side crashing out in the last 16 against Spain, when Mikel Merino netted a last-minute winner.

Now, the curtain has come down on his international journey, just weeks after his historic rival Lionel Messi did the same with Argentina.

He had been suspended by the Portuguese FA last month for 30 days, as well as receiving a £215 fine, after storming out of the Nations League camp having fallen out with manager Jorge Jesus.

In an emotional five-minute video posted to his social media channels, Ronaldo addressed the Portuguese people.

"To the Portuguese people, the day has come to hand back the shirt and the captain's armband of the national team that belongs to all of us,” he began.

"I never felt that it was exclusively mine, but for 23 years, I had the privilege and responsibility of wearing it, defending it, and carrying it with me to stadiums all around the world.

"Today, the moment has come to pass it on to the future.

"It was not an easy decision, because some decisions are not made with the head alone. They are also made with the heart.

Ronaldo makes bombshell retirement decision after Portugal suspension

Glazer risks Man Utd fan fury with bold claim in rare public interview
